inputs: Public Form 5500 filings and available Schedule A/C records, employer size and plan-year information, employer-confirmed renewal dates and appropriately obtained business contact details.

Employer authorization, incumbent fee disclosures, plan documents, aggregate claims and pharmacy reports, stop-loss terms, underwriting requirements and privacy-controlled access to necessary participant information.

Licensed broker and specialist relationships, TPA and stop-loss proposals, captive participation terms, PBM rebate and spread definitions, NADAC availability and fallback pricing rules, and a $40–$65 PEPM service proposal.
operator_plays.mechanism: Use public Form 5500 Schedule A/C information, where filed and informative, to identify mid-market renewal and compensation-review opportunities, then offer an employer-authorized CAA 2021 service-provider fee-disclosure review. A properly licensed advisory team can seek broker-of-record appointments and compare bundled coverage with separately contracted TPA, stop-loss or suitable captive arrangements and a transparent pass-through PBM using an explicitly defined NADAC-based pricing methodology. Negotiate recurring $40–$65 PEPM advisory fees where supported by scope and client agreement, with all commissions and indirect compensation disclosed and no assumption that unbundling guarantees savings.
metrics: Recurring advisory revenue: enrolled employees multiplied by the contracted $40–$65 PEPM fee, less servicing costs and disclosed fee offsets.
Risk-adjusted employer cost: claims, administration, stop-loss premiums, pharmacy costs, collateral and runout obligations minus realized rebates and recoveries.
Service and retention quality: renewal retention, disclosure completeness, pharmacy guarantee reconciliation variance and unresolved participant access issues.
operator_plays.name: Mid-Market Level-Funded Benefits and Transparent PBM Advisory Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Adverse-scenario funding gap, claims-to-budget variance, unrecovered stop-loss balances and unexplained differences between disclosed and received compensation.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The proposed unbundled plan produces adverse claims exposure or undisclosed compensation despite appearing cheaper on headline premiums.
platform_risks.fallback: Retain or competitively rebid the existing structure when risk-adjusted economics are unfavorable, obtain explicit pricing fallbacks and narrow the engagement to disclosed advisory work until implementation conditions are satisfied.
platform_risks.impact: Employer costs exceed projections, coverage continuity deteriorates and advisory fees or the BOR relationship become disputed.
platform_risks.trigger: Incomplete claims data, stop-loss lasers or exclusions, nonrefundable captive collateral, ambiguous PBM rebate definitions or unsupported NADAC pricing for uncovered products.

workflow: 1. Analyze publicly available filings through permitted access methods, identify likely renewal opportunities and confirm current plan arrangements directly because filings are historical and may omit relevant compensation details.
2. Obtain employer authorization, review applicable CAA 2021 disclosures and existing termination terms, and define advisory deliverables and compensation before requesting any BOR appointment.

3. Compare fully insured and level-funded options using expected and adverse claims scenarios, stop-loss exclusions and lasers, captive collateral, TPA fees, pharmacy guarantees and rebates actually retained by the employer.

4. Implement the employer-selected structure with licensed parties, privacy safeguards and continuity planning; collect agreed PEPM fees and review total costs, disclosures and service performance at each renewal.

inputs: Customer authorization, three to four years of policies and premium audits, payroll registers, job-duty evidence, overtime breakdowns, officer election documents and subcontractor coverage records.
Applicable state classification rules, NCCI or independent-bureau worksheets, experience-period and valuation dates, carrier loss runs and documented claim corrections.
Carrier and bureau dispute procedures, policy-specific correction deadlines, a 30%–40% realized-refund agreement and licensed brokerage support for any BOR renewal engagement.
operator_plays.mechanism: Audit three to four historical policy years where carrier, state and rating-bureau correction rules permit, checking actual duties, payroll classifications, eligible overtime adjustments and officer exclusions or limits. Reconcile NCCI experience-rating worksheets, or the applicable independent bureau's equivalent, to accurate carrier loss reports and valuation dates; an open reserve is not an error merely because the ultimate claim later costs less. Recover documented premium overpayments for a negotiated 30%–40% contingency and pursue separately authorized, properly licensed BOR renewal work.
metrics: Realized premium recovery: received refunds and usable policy credits divided by audited historical premium, segmented by payroll, classification and experience-mod correction.
Correction conversion: dollars recovered divided by dollars submitted, alongside days from supported dispute to revised audit or bureau worksheet.
Renewal economics: separately disclosed brokerage revenue and verified prospective premium effect, controlling for payroll, operations, rates and coverage changes.
operator_plays.name: Workers' Compensation Classification and Experience-Mod Recovery Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Rejected correction dollars by reason, percentage of payroll supported by contemporaneous records and net premium change after the full audit.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A carrier or rating bureau rejects proposed corrections because classifications, loss valuations or retroactive deadlines were misinterpreted.
platform_risks.fallback: Withdraw unsupported claims, disclose any additional premium exposure, use the bureau's documented dispute process for defensible items and improve prospective payroll and claims reporting.
platform_risks.impact: No refund is issued, advisory effort is unrecovered and a broader audit may identify additional premium owed.
platform_risks.trigger: Unsupported separation of payroll, missing officer elections, treatment of later reserve reductions as historical errors or submission outside the permitted correction period.

workflow: 1. Map each policy to its governing state and bureau rules, establish the allowable correction window and reconcile audited payroll to contemporaneous employment and job-duty records.
2. Test class-code assignments, permitted overtime premium exclusions, officer elections or payroll limits and subcontractor treatment without relabeling work merely to obtain a cheaper rate.
3. Reconcile experience-mod inputs against losses reported for the applicable valuation date; submit evidenced payroll, classification or loss-data corrections to the carrier and bureau as required.
4. Obtain revised audits or rating worksheets, trace resulting premium credits through endorsements and receipts, collect the 30%–40% contingency and separately quote licensed BOR renewal services.

operator_plays.name: Private B2B Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) Umbrella & Contingent Spend-Audit Arbitrage
operator_plays.mechanism: Pool 10,000–75,000+ seats and indirect corporate spend across hundreds of SMB member companies under authorized master GPO volume brackets through Una, OMNIA or private vertical SaaS, parcel and telecom GPOs. Pair negotiated brackets with quarter-end vendor price-floor benchmarking informed by Vendr/Tropic playbooks, targeting 3%–12% vendor-paid administrative rebates and 25%–35% contingent Year-1 shared-savings splits under no savings, no fee agreements. Eligibility, rebate bases and benchmark access must be verified; disclose dual compensation and avoid double-counting rebates in client savings.
inputs: Executed GPO member and supplier agreements defining eligible aggregated spend, volume brackets, administrative rebates and compensation disclosures
Member-authorized invoices and seat inventories plus lawfully obtained, like-for-like Vendr/Tropic-style pricing benchmarks
Contingent audit contracts defining the Year-1 savings baseline, exclusions, 25%–35% fee schedule and independent reconciliation rights
workflow: 1. Enroll eligible SMB members with written authority and aggregate verified seat demand and indirect spend without exchanging competitively sensitive data.
2. Validate GPO purchasing eligibility and negotiate supplier volume brackets using lawful quarter-end benchmarks for comparable service and commitment terms.
3. Present disclosed vendor rebates and contingent fees, secure member approval and implement authorized contract changes against an agreed savings baseline.
4. Reconcile actual Year-1 savings and vendor rebates, charge only earned shared-savings fees and audit bracket eligibility and renewal pricing.
metrics: Verified eligible seats and annual member spend within contracted GPO brackets
Realized Year-1 member savings net of contingent fees on a normalized baseline
Collected administrative rebates and shared-savings fees net of reversals

positioning_alternatives.subtitle: Convert documented payroll-code and experience-rating errors into carrier-approved corrections and collected contingent fee splits.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40 holds Rank #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score by converting opaque benefits compensation, pharmacy contracts, and workers' compensation rating errors into documented advisory income. This chapter maps 11 operating plays across five specialist archetypes, separating repeatable execution from speculative savings claims. Operator revenue means net retained PEPM fees, earned stop-loss/TPA commissions, and supportable contingent refund splits; employer claims, premiums, and purchasing volume remain outside that boundary. Canonical annual owner profit is $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled. Durable operators combine licensed distribution, reproducible contract analysis, secure claims handling, and correction evidence. They retain existing coverage whenever transition economics fail and collect contingent fees only against the agreed, verified recovery basis.

sections.heading: 1. Sell documented contract correction, not ownership of employer claim dollars
paragraphs: Self-funded health, PBM, and workers' compensation arbitrage is a licensed advisory and brokerage business that earns money by correcting contract opacity, procurement friction, and rating errors. The operator does not buy an employer's medical liabilities cheaply and resell them. An employer sponsors its health plan, a third-party administrator processes claims, a pharmacy benefit manager administers prescriptions, and a stop-loss insurer reimburses covered losses above negotiated attachment points. Separately, workers' compensation insurers price occupational injury coverage using payroll classifications, experience-rating inputs, and jurisdiction-specific rules. The operator earns disclosed advisory fees, placement compensation, or a contracted share of verified recoveries. A broker-of-record appointment changes representation under carrier rules; it neither transfers plan assets nor automatically creates commission rights. Candidate #40's edge is coordinating specialists around evidence that employers rarely assemble themselves. Its 93/100 score comprises revenue potential 25, profit-margin potential 24, team efficiency 19, startup accessibility 13, and automation potential 12. Those scores describe the opportunity's operating shape, not a client's expected savings. The practical product is a defensible decision package with executable contracts, identified counterparties, a measurement baseline, and clearly allocated responsibility for each implementation task and subsequent service failure.

The recognition boundary must survive a bank reconciliation. A client with 500 billed employees at $55 per employee per month produces $330,000 of annual advisory consideration when all twelve service months are delivered. Its several million dollars of claims and insurance premiums are neither operator sales nor a revenue multiple denominator. Count stop-loss or TPA commissions only under actual appointment, licensing, service, and carrier compensation terms. A $200,000 workers' compensation refund with a contracted 30% recovery fee creates $60,000 of potential operator consideration, not $200,000 of sales. Under ASC 606, assess each promised service and whether the operator controls it before transfer; principal-versus-agent presentation is not an elective shortcut. This scorecard uses net retained operator consideration, excluding amounts collected for counterparties. An operator acting as principal must separately reconcile its reporting presentation to that management measure. Recurring service fees generally follow service delivery; commissions follow the identified performance obligation and applicable reversal assessment. Recovery fees remain constrained while entitlement or amount could materially reverse. Cash receipt, a favorable worksheet, and a carrier promise are different events. Maintain separate schedules for earned consideration, receivables, deferred collections, partner allocations, and potential chargebacks.

Five archetypes keep the small team focused. The renewal advisor sources employers and evaluates bundled versus separately contracted arrangements. The pharmacy specialist reconstructs ingredient pricing, dispensing charges, rebates, and exclusions. The stop-loss specialist translates claim volatility into specific and aggregate protection. The experience-rating specialist traces payroll and losses into bureau calculations and carrier corrections. The purchasing specialist aggregates eligible indirect spend without pretending that every member qualifies for every supplier bracket. This chapter maps 11 plays across those archetypes; the comparison matrix identifies the two specified catalog plays and nine concrete operating extensions rather than inventing additional catalog IDs. Startup capital of $8,000–$45,000 covers licensing, errors and omissions coverage, secure systems, specialist contracting, and acquisition work. The $2,000–$11,000 monthly opex range is a planning envelope for recurring operating overhead, not an all-inclusive expense cap at every scale. Contract labor, acquisition costs, variable servicing, and other modeled expenses must also be reconciled. A first deal in two to five months depends on renewal timing and usable employer records. Begin with one repeatable archetype and named specialist coverage for the others; trying to administer claims, place insurance, litigate balance bills, and audit every payroll code personally destroys the manpower advantage.

sections.heading: 2. Map eleven plays to measurable units and explicit fallback routes
paragraphs: The catalog play erisa_level_funded_transparent_pbm_bor_arbitrage begins with public Form 5500 information, not a purchased list of supposedly distressed employers. Use Schedule A insurance information and Schedule C service-provider information only where filed, relevant, and informative; filing exemptions and welfare-plan reporting rules leave real gaps. Reconcile plan identifiers, filing year, insurer names, and available contract dates, then verify the actual renewal with the employer. Request an employer-authorized CAA 2021 compensation review before recommending a broker-of-record change. At 200 contracted employees, $40–$65 PEPM supports $96,000–$156,000 annually for a genuinely specified advisory scope. Those fees are negotiated targets, not a statutory entitlement or universal market price. Compare the incumbent bundle against separate TPA, stop-loss, network, and PBM contracts, including implementation charges and replacement broker compensation. A level-funded arrangement commonly combines fixed payments with a self-funded claim component; its label alone does not resolve legal or economic classification. Suitable captive participation requires additional examination of collateral, assessments, withdrawal terms, and member risk. Retain or competitively rebid the incumbent structure if risk-adjusted economics deteriorate. Until contract conditions are satisfied, limit work to disclosed advisory services rather than promising a transition date.

Transparent pharmacy procurement requires a written pricing formula. CMS NADAC is a survey-based acquisition-cost benchmark for covered outpatient drugs, not a universal transaction price or a complete specialty formulary. Define NDC matching, quantity units, benchmark publication date, update frequency, dispensing fees, ingredient adjustments, and treatment of reversals. Explicitly price drugs without a usable NADAC record instead of silently substituting an optimistic benchmark. For 100,000 comparable fills, reducing net cost by an illustrated $3 per fill yields $300,000 of employer savings before transition charges and other changes; it does not create $300,000 of operator revenue. Separate manufacturer rebates, PBM guarantees, administrative credits, and pharmacy reimbursements so the same dollar cannot appear twice. Compare formulary changes and specialty access as well as price. A rebate recovery requires contractual entitlement, paid-claim eligibility, settlement periods, and audit access; an advertised pass-through percentage proves none of these. The adjacent workers' compensation plays are similarly evidence-bound. If a simplified premium component of $400,000 changes from a 1.20 modifier to 1.10, the indicated difference is $40,000 before other rating adjustments. Only carrier endorsements and billing reconciliation establish the actual refund. Hold contingent invoices when bureau acceptance, policy application, or recovery remains disputed.

The second catalog play, private_b2b_gpo_umbrella_rebate_arbitrage, is an adjacent employer-distribution opportunity rather than health-plan claim revenue. Pool 10,000–75,000+ eligible seats and indirect spend across hundreds of SMB members through authorized Una, OMNIA, or private vertical purchasing agreements. Verify whether the particular supplier and agreement accept private employers; public purchasing contracts do not automatically extend to them. Use authorized contract information and Vendr or Tropic procurement methods to challenge renewal price floors, without claiming access to proprietary benchmark feeds. A target 3%–12% supplier administration rebate on $1,000,000 of eligible settled spend would produce $30,000–$120,000 before member allocations, retention terms, and reversals. A separate 25%–35% Year-1 fee on $100,000 of verified incremental savings would produce $25,000–$35,000. These are conditional negotiation illustrations, not standard platform offers or additions to the canonical scorecard. Disclose dual compensation, agree whether supplier rebates reduce the savings-fee base, and separate price reductions from volume changes. If eligibility or the baseline fails, suspend disputed fees, reconcile with members and suppliers, refund unearned amounts, and move affected members to eligible agreements. The matrix distinguishes eleven monetizable plays from five supporting contract workstreams.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile every scenario to retained revenue and fully loaded delivery costs
paragraphs: Formula v2.0 provides three fixed annual operating cases. The following revenue bridges are illustrative compositions that reconcile exactly to those totals, not additional engine inputs or claims about an existing book. Conservative combines 150 billed employees at $40 PEPM for twelve months, producing $72,000, with $30,000 of earned retained stop-loss/TPA commissions and $18,000 of recognized contingent recovery fees. Total operator revenue is $120,000. At a 32% net margin, modeled expenses are $81,600 and annual owner net profit is $38,400. The team is one full-time operator and three contractors, not four full-time salaries. Contractor engagements must specify actual hours or deliverables and their cost. A plausible division assigns licensed placement support, pharmacy analysis, and payroll/rating review to specialists while the owner handles employer relationships and contract coordination. Commission amounts in this bridge are after relevant third-party agency allocations; expenses still include the operator's own delivery costs. If an agreement instead requires gross presentation, keep a separate bridge to the retained scorecard basis. Do not apply a second retained-share haircut to amounts already stated as retained. No additional numeric retained-share assumption is supplied by the canonical specification.

Base combines 500 billed employees at $55 PEPM for twelve months, or $330,000, with $125,000 of retained commissions and $80,000 of recognized recovery fees. The result is $535,000 of revenue, $294,250 of modeled expenses, and $240,750 of annual owner net profit at 45.0%. The staffing count remains one full-time operator plus three contractors, so the operating change is larger standardized engagements and better specialist utilization, not invisible free labor. Scaled combines 900 billed employees at $65 PEPM, or $702,000, with $160,000 of retained commissions and $88,000 of recovery fees. Revenue reaches $950,000; expenses equal $399,000; annual owner net profit is $551,000 at 58%. Two full-time staff and four contractors make six people. These arithmetic bridges assume all twelve contracted service months are earned; a midyear start requires proration. Fee levels must correspond to employer-approved scope and disclosed total compensation. The margin expansion depends on repeatable analysis, controlled acquisition spending, and lower service effort per covered employee. It disappears if complex claim disputes, manual reporting, or repeated implementation failures consume the anticipated productivity gains. Do not add the GPO illustration to any of these totals.

A profitable annual model can still run short of cash. PEPM invoices may settle monthly while carrier commissions arrive after premium payment and recovery fees remain unearned during correction disputes. Maintain a thirteen-week cash forecast separating contracted recurring collections, carrier remittances, contingent receipts, and contractor obligations. The cited monthly overhead envelope cannot substitute for the full annual expense bridge: Base expenses average approximately $24,520.83 monthly, including costs beyond recurring overhead. Scaled expenses average $33,250 monthly. Treat owner net profit as the scorecard's business-level residual, not a statement of personal after-tax cash or a separately specified owner salary. Document the treatment of owner compensation before comparing this model with another business. Stress-test employer concentration with actual contracts: losing 100 Base employees removes $66,000 of annual advisory revenue before any associated commission changes. A $20,000 clawback reduces profit dollar-for-dollar absent offsetting costs or replacement income. Keep scenario outputs unchanged and present such sensitivities separately. Establish receivable aging, refund authority, and reserve methodology before hiring against contingent awards. The durable small-team moat is reliable retained contribution after servicing and reversals, not the largest premium number displayed in a proposal.

sections.heading: 4. Build the moat around permissioned evidence, contractual authority, and recoverable errors
paragraphs: Authority is activity-specific. Maintain active state Life & Health and Property & Casualty producer licenses for the insurance work performed, with required agency licenses and carrier appointments. TPA licensing is a separate inquiry when an operator administers coverage or claims; a producer license does not settle it. ERISA preemption does not erase state insurance requirements, and 29 U.S.C. §1144 preserves important insurance-law boundaries. Texas Insurance Code Chapter 4151 illustrates a distinct administrator regime. Under 29 U.S.C. §1108(b)(2)(B), covered group-health brokerage and consulting arrangements meeting the statutory compensation threshold require specified disclosures about services, fiduciary status where applicable, and direct and indirect compensation. Deliver the required information reasonably before entering, extending, or renewing the arrangement, and manage subsequent changes under the applicable timing rules. The employer's fiduciary process under 29 U.S.C. §1104 must evaluate reasonable compensation and prudent selection. A disclosure does not cure every conflict or turn unnecessary services into reasonable expenses. Avoid receiving employer claim funds merely to create a larger revenue narrative. Contracts should specify who holds funds, who pays claims, who owns records, and how the employer retrieves usable information after termination without disrupting member coverage or insurer reimbursement.

Claims access creates a security and workflow obligation. Where the operator acts as a business associate, execute appropriate agreements under 45 CFR §164.504(e), apply the minimum-necessary standard where required by §164.502(b), and implement the applicable Security Rule controls. Use role-based access, multifactor authentication, encryption, auditable exports, and a documented retention schedule rather than ordinary email attachments containing member-level claims. Separate public Form 5500 prospecting records from restricted claim and eligibility records. Automate public renewal targeting with filing-date checks and source attribution, NADAC repricing with versioned benchmark files and exception reports, and NCCI or payroll analysis with employer-authorized records and jurisdiction-specific rules. These automations recommend questions; they do not decide licensure, carrier underwriting, bureau corrections, or disputed contractual entitlement. Require an analyst to trace sample results back to original records before proposals leave the firm. Workers' compensation claim disclosures have distinct HIPAA treatment under §164.512(l); do not assume that exception makes all employer medical information freely shareable. The moat is a reproducible evidence chain that a new specialist can inspect, not an undocumented spreadsheet controlled by one founder. Preserve contract versions and dated approvals alongside each calculation so later audits can reproduce the decision.

Transition risk deserves the same attention as quoted savings. Specific stop-loss protects against individual claim severity, while aggregate protection addresses covered claim totals under its own definitions. A laser can impose a higher individual attachment or exclusion; a lower premium may therefore purchase materially less protection. Model incurred and paid windows, run-in exposure, run-out administration, reimbursement lag, and termination obligations across both old and new contracts. Reference-based pricing introduces provider collection and member balance-bill exposure; identify who supplies defense, funds settlements, and coordinates disputes. Federal surprise-billing protections, including 42 U.S.C. §300gg-111, cover defined circumstances rather than every out-of-network bill. Likewise, a corrected workers' compensation worksheet does not automatically reopen every historical policy. Check bureau rules, carrier endorsement procedures, and applicable dispute periods before offering a contingent engagement. Incumbent brokers will defend renewals with revised pricing, service promises, and commission changes; compare the revised written offer rather than treating retention as a lost sale. A disciplined operator can earn disclosed advisory income while recommending no change. Finish each engagement with a decision record, accepted implementation responsibilities, a billing reconciliation schedule, and an exit plan. These artifacts convert one-time analysis into defensible recurring service without requiring a large internal workforce.

chapters.question_prompt: Who writes the check in self-funded health, pbm & workers' comp arbitrage, what acute financial or statutory pain forces them to pay, and how do funds clear cleanly without circumvention or non-payment?
chapters.title: Who Pays, Why They Pay & How the Payment Rail Works
chapters.subtitle: Employer Treasury, ERISA Section 408(b)(2), PBM Rebate Ledgers, Stop-Loss Commissions and NCCI Premium-Refund Settlement
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40, Self-Funded Health, PBM & Workers' Comp Arbitrage, ranks #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 11 mapped plays monetize employer purchasing friction, benefit-contract opacity, and documented premium errors through retained advisory fees, disclosed commissions, and earned recovery splits. The economic buyer is usually the employer CFO; the payment authority may instead sit with treasury, a plan fiduciary, or a carrier commission department. This chapter separates those authorities, compares eight payment arrangements, and makes collection depend on evidence rather than introductions. Canonical annual owner profit is $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled. Employer claim funds, insurance premiums, rebate principal, and recovered premium remain outside operator revenue; only the contracted, retained fee enters the scorecard.

sections.heading: 1. Identify the economic buyer, the authorized payer and the loss they cannot ignore
paragraphs: Sell first to the person accountable for the expense, then identify the person legally authorized to release money. At a mid-market employer, the CFO usually owns the health-benefit and workers' compensation budget; human resources owns employee disruption; treasury controls ACH enrollment; and the plan committee may control decisions involving plan assets. These roles overlap, but they are not interchangeable. A benefits director can sponsor an audit without authority to bind the company, direct a trust distribution, or replace a producer. Obtain the contracting entity's legal name, signatory authority, purchase-order requirements, invoice destination, and bank-verification procedure before accepting sensitive records. Ask whether fees will come from corporate operating cash or a plan account. ERISA fiduciary duties under 29 U.S.C. 1104 and prohibited-transaction rules under 29 U.S.C. 1106 make that distinction operationally important. Employer business expenses cannot simply be routed through plan assets because cash is available there. The immediate buying trigger is usually an unbudgeted renewal increase, an opaque pharmacy reconciliation, a disputed premium audit, or a stop-loss exclusion. Translate each trigger into an approved expense category and a documented payment obligation, not a promise that savings will eventually finance everything.

Organize the 11 mapped plays into buying problems rather than presenting eleven unrelated services. Self-funded feasibility, captive participation, specific stop-loss design, aggregate protection, and TPA fee review address renewal volatility. PBM spread repricing and rebate recovery address opaque pharmacy economics. Reference-based pricing support addresses provider-payment execution. Form 5500 renewal targeting creates qualified opportunities rather than independent client revenue. Historical workers' compensation recovery and separately authorized broker-of-record renewal work address premium leakage and future placement. For a 500-employee account, an illustrative $12 PEPM advisory agreement produces $6,000 monthly and $72,000 annually, not the employer's multimillion-dollar claim spend. A $2 reduction across 20,000 comparable prescriptions suggests $40,000 of potential purchasing improvement, but it does not establish collected rebates or earned contingent fees. The CFO wants defensible cash impact; human resources wants continuity; procurement wants contractual accountability. Show all three a baseline, implementation cost, owner, and fallback. If a stop-loss laser removes the expected advantage, retain the existing structure while renegotiating specific terms. If pharmacy repricing lacks usable claim-level records, sell a bounded data-and-contract review instead of projecting recovery. One client can buy several workstreams, but overlapping work must not create duplicate charges or duplicate savings claims.

Screen willingness and ability to pay separately. An employer can be profitable yet refuse an invoice because procurement never onboarded the supplier; another can approve the work while lacking liquidity at settlement. Review public bankruptcy records through PACER, secretary-of-state entity status, available trade references, and financial statements supplied with permission. For larger contingent exposures, inspect current liquidity, debt restrictions, related-party dependencies, and whether a parent actually guarantees payment. An entity search does not establish solvency, and a UCC filing is a financing signal rather than proof of distress. Request a named accounts-payable contact and a sample remittance process before kickoff. Use a modest corporate-funded retainer for research-heavy engagements, shorter billing intervals for thinly capitalized employers, and a documented stop-work right for delinquent advisory invoices. Never suspend participant claims administration or hold health records hostage to collect a consulting fee. For commission income, screen the carrier or intermediary separately: confirm appointment, commission schedule, producer-of-record status, cancellation treatment, and statement timing. A solvent employer does not cure an uncollectible commission promise from an unauthorized introducer. Record the actual obligor for every revenue line so treasury can pursue the right counterparty.

sections.heading: 2. Select the payment arrangement without taking custody of employer money
paragraphs: Treat payment method, payment condition, and custody as separate design choices. Wire and ACH move money; retainers and milestone holds define when it becomes payable; escrow appoints a custodian; factoring changes who purchases a receivable. Statutory disbursement is a constrained distribution process, not a universal payment network. Platform checkout is an interface over card or bank rails. The comparison below therefore evaluates eight commercial arrangements without pretending they provide identical protections. Default to corporate ACH for recurring advisory invoices and independently verified wire instructions for unusually large settlements. ACH authorization must identify the account holder, amount or calculation method, timing, and revocation procedure. Confirm business-account rules and bank deadlines rather than importing consumer protections into a corporate contract. Neither a screenshot nor a pending bank entry proves final collection. Reconcile the bank posting, invoice, and remittance reference, and handle returns or reversals under the actual bank agreement. For wires, verify changed instructions through an established telephone number, never the number included in the change request. A compromised email can redirect an otherwise legitimate payment faster than a contract clause can recover it. Keep initiation and bank-detail approval with different authorized people.

Keep claim funding and premium payments outside the advisory operating account. Employers fund the TPA or insurer under their existing agreements; carriers pay recognized producer commissions under appointment terms; PBMs remit rebates to the contractually entitled recipient; and carriers return premium overpayments to the insured or other entitled payee. The operator then invoices its earned fee against the documented event. A direction-to-pay letter can simplify administration only when the payer accepts it and the arrangement respects ownership, licensing, and applicable asset restrictions. It does not automatically assign funds or make the carrier responsible for the employer's consulting debt. For a $100,000 accepted premium refund at a 35% contingency, the employer receives $100,000 and owes $35,000 under the engagement; the operator does not book $100,000 and later expense $65,000. If a permitted independent escrow handles both distributions, require written release conditions, verified beneficiary details, segregated records, and a dispute mechanism. Do not call an ordinary operating account escrow. Where a recovery belongs to a plan or includes participant interests, establish ownership and permissible expense allocation before distribution. Employer convenience alone cannot convert plan money into unrestricted corporate cash.

Build the recurring payment schedule around observable work and the contingent schedule around observable collection. A $6,000 monthly advisory fee can be billed in advance against a defined service period, with termination and any unused-fee treatment stated explicitly. That billing timing does not itself determine revenue recognition. A recovery fee should distinguish cash refunds, applied credits, disputed credits, and future renewal reductions. If a carrier applies a $40,000 credit against a payable premium installment and the contract treats realized credits as recovery, a 35% fee equals $14,000 once the credit is actually applied and evidenced. A proposed worksheet adjustment alone does not trigger that result. Use milestone holds for a contested portion while releasing undisputed compensation; define the reviewer, evidence deadline, and escalation path. Factoring should be a last-mile liquidity decision for an assignable, earned receivable, not a device for financing speculative savings. A 3% purchase discount on a $20,000 invoice costs $600 before other charges; recourse can leave collection risk with the operator. Platform checkout suits small corporate retainers, but processor fees, card disputes, and transaction limits can make it unsuitable for large contingent settlements.

sections.heading: 3. Protect the fee with evidence, scoped authority and defensible recovery math
paragraphs: The play workers_comp_ncci_emod_retroactive_recovery begins with a signed historical-audit scope, not a blanket claim that every high experience modifier is wrong. Audit three to four historical policy years only where carrier, state, and rating-bureau correction rules permit. Compare actual job duties with applicable classifications, reconcile payroll to audited exposures, test eligible overtime adjustments, and check officer exclusions or limits against the governing state rules and policy elections. Reconcile NCCI experience-rating worksheets, or the applicable independent bureau's equivalent, to accurate carrier loss reports and valuation dates. An open reserve is not an error merely because the ultimate claim later costs less. Build an issue register showing policy, disputed item, governing rule, source document, proposed correction, and possible adverse adjustment. A documented $200,000 collected premium overpayment at 35% produces a $70,000 operator fee and leaves $130,000 with the employer before any separately agreed expenses. The permitted commercial range here is a negotiated 30%–40%, subject to the actual engagement and applicable state requirements. Withdraw unsupported claims, disclose additional premium exposure, use the bureau's documented dispute process for defensible items, and improve prospective payroll and claims reporting when historical correction is unavailable.

Protect payment by defining attribution narrowly enough to survive a real dispute. Attach the initial issue register and identify preexisting carrier disputes so the operator cannot claim credit for someone else's completed work. State whether the fee applies to cash, realized premium credits, or both; describe netting for offsetting additional premiums arising from the same accepted correction. For example, a $60,000 refund accompanied by a related $10,000 additional premium produces a $50,000 net recovery and a $17,500 fee at 35% if that is the agreed basis. Give the client a reporting duty for carrier correspondence and settlements, reasonable access to supporting statements, and a limited post-termination tail covering identified work already delivered. Avoid a perpetual claim over every future premium reduction. A targeted noncircumvention clause should preserve payment for documented work without preventing the employer from speaking to its carrier. Separate recovery authority from broker-of-record authority: obtaining records does not appoint a producer, and a renewal appointment does not create historical contingency rights. When the client disputes attribution, collect the undisputed portion and use the agreed review process rather than interfering with coverage or threatening essential benefits operations.

Licensing and disclosure determine whether an otherwise attractive fee can be retained. Verify active state Life and Health authority for applicable benefits sales and Property and Casualty authority for workers' compensation placement, including entity licenses, appointments, and nonresident requirements where relevant. Determine separately whether specific administration functions require TPA authority; a consulting label does not change the activity performed. Texas Insurance Code Sections 4001.051 and 4151.051 illustrate separate agent and administrator frameworks, subject to their definitions and exceptions. For covered group-health brokerage or consulting arrangements expecting at least $1,000 in direct or indirect compensation, apply ERISA Section 408(b)(2)(B), codified at 29 U.S.C. 1108(b)(2)(B), including required advance disclosures and applicable update obligations. Explain commissions, overrides, referral payments, and termination-related compensation in the actual arrangement. Disclosure does not replace the requirement that compensation be reasonable. Before receiving protected health information as a business associate, execute the required agreement and implement role-based access. For PBM records, confirm audit rights and applicable gag-clause restrictions rather than assuming a broker appointment unlocks every field. Keep stop-loss run-out terms, reference-based pricing defense arrangements, and carrier reimbursement conditions visible because collection economics deteriorate when promised implementation cannot actually be delivered.

sections.heading: 4. Reconcile the retained-fee ledger to all three canonical operating cases
paragraphs: Use the scorecard's annual revenue totals as retained operator revenue, even though the scenario metadata calls them gross revenue. They are not gross employer billings, claim disbursements, premium volume, or rebate principal. Under the stated retained-share basis, amounts belonging to other parties remain outside the operator's revenue bridge. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to the actual contracts rather than assuming every commission or pass-through arrangement has identical accounting. The following unit bridges are illustrative compositions of the supplied totals, not additional scorecard outputs. Conservative uses 1,000 average billed employees at $8 PEPM for twelve months, producing $96,000, plus $12,000 retained commissions and $12,000 recovery fees from $40,000 recovered at 30%. Total revenue is exactly $120,000. At 32% net margin, owner net profit is $38,400 and total modeled costs are $81,600. Staffing remains 1 FT + 3 C. Count only billable employee months actually covered by the agreement; dependents are not additional employees unless the contract explicitly uses another billing unit. A partial-year launch cannot claim twelve months of PEPM revenue merely because the signed client census reaches the illustrative year-end headcount. Reconcile monthly census changes before invoicing.

Base uses 2,500 average billed employees at $12 PEPM for twelve months, producing $360,000, plus $105,000 retained commissions and $70,000 recovery fees from $200,000 recovered at 35%. Total revenue is $535,000; the 45.0% margin produces $240,750 owner net profit and $294,250 total modeled costs with 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled uses 4,000 average billed employees at $15 PEPM for twelve months, producing $720,000, plus $125,000 retained commissions and $105,000 recovery fees from $300,000 recovered at 35%. Total revenue is $950,000; the 58% margin produces $551,000 owner net profit and $399,000 total modeled costs with 2 FT + 4 C. These bridges assume the fees and commissions are separately earned, disclosed where required, and not contractually offset against each other. If an advisory agreement credits commissions against PEPM fees, subtract that credit instead of counting both amounts. The rising margins are canonical scenario assumptions, not results established by these unit examples. Validate delivery capacity, contractor expense, acquisition cost, insurance, software, and collection losses against the full cost envelope. Do not treat the narrower monthly overhead range as the entire annual expense model.

Run a settlement ledger beside the revenue ledger because earned fees and available cash diverge. Each recovery entry should identify the client, policy period, accepted correction, gross refund, related offset, realized credit, contingency rate, invoice date, due date, and collected fee. Each commission entry needs carrier statement references, applicable revenue-sharing deductions, cancellation exposure, and any client fee credit. For recurring advisory work, tie invoices to the agreed employee-month census and service period. A 30-day payment delay on $60,000 of valid invoices creates a $60,000 working-capital gap without automatically changing recognized revenue; a $6,000 unrecoverable balance reduces economic profit unless already included in the cost assumptions. Maintain an aging review that separates administrative delays, disputed scope, counterparty distress, and confirmed bank returns. Escalate administrative delays to accounts payable, scope disputes to the named reviewer, and deteriorating credit to revised terms for future work. Keep recovered employer money out of operator cash forecasts except for the earned retained fee. Close each month by reconciling contracts, source statements, invoices, bank receipts, and outstanding disputes. This discipline makes the small-team model collectible without turning the advisory business into an unlicensed custodian or an involuntary lender.

chapters.question_prompt: What are the real unit economics, gross-to-net margin deductions, scrub/reversal reserves, and working-capital float requirements for self-funded health, pbm & workers' comp arbitrage?
chapters.title: Unit Economics, Margin Waterfall & Working-Capital Float
chapters.subtitle: Retained PEPM Fees, ERISA Compensation Disclosures, PBM Recovery Scrubs, NCCI Corrections & Stop-Loss Commission Collection
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40, Self-Funded Health, PBM & Workers' Comp Arbitrage, holds Rank #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 11 mapped plays. Its economics depend on retained advisory compensation, not employer claims, premiums, or advertised drug savings. The canonical annual owner profits are $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled, supported by recognized operator revenue of $120,000, $535,000, and $950,000. This chapter reconciles those outcomes through explicit producer splits, reversal allowances, contractor delivery, acquisition spending, and overhead. It also separates accounting margin from collection timing: illustrative funding envelopes reach $26,400, $122,083.33, and $208,250. Specialty-drug sourcing remains outside committed revenue until the actual product, distribution pathway, contract, and collectible savings satisfy documented operating requirements.

sections.heading: 1. Define the retained revenue unit before pricing the employer cohort
paragraphs: Start with a signed employer relationship, not a claims-dollar opportunity. Candidate #40's canonical revenue basis is retained PEPM advisory fees, stop-loss or TPA commissions, and earned Workers' Comp recovery splits. Employer medical claims, pharmacy expenditure, insurance premiums, and payroll are measurement inputs, never operator sales. For this bridge, one cohort means one employer account with twelve service months; all three cases represent annualized operating states rather than first-year booking forecasts. Conservative uses six employers averaging 150 covered employees; Base uses fifteen averaging 250; Scaled uses twenty averaging 400. At $8 PEPM, recurring advisory revenue becomes $86,400, $360,000, and $768,000. Add retained placement compensation of $24,000, $120,000, and $140,000, plus collected-and-earned recovery fees of $9,600, $55,000, and $42,000. Those sums reproduce $120,000, $535,000, and $950,000 exactly. These are illustrative component allocations, not additional scorecard inputs or representations about prevailing market prices. The lower Scaled recovery allocation deliberately prevents uncertain retrospective refunds from carrying the growth thesis. Count covered employees consistently: dependents, eligible workers, enrolled workers, and enrolled contracts are different denominators. Preserve the contractual denominator in every invoice and retain monthly enrollment snapshots for later billing reconciliation.

Separate the retained-revenue composition from the upstream compensation statement. Illustrative gross contractual fee and commission entitlements are $150,000, $650,000, and $1,150,000. Deduct external producer allocations of $24,000, $91,000, and $158,000, then variable consideration allowances of $6,000, $24,000, and $42,000. The remaining recognized amounts again equal the canonical revenue totals. Under this illustration, the operator arranges the externally allocated services as agent; that accounting conclusion requires the actual control and contract analysis under ASC 606. A principal presentation could instead place a provider payment in expense, without changing underlying retained economics. Do not apply another retained-share haircut to the canonical totals: they already represent the retained operator basis. Equally, do not subtract the allowance again when calculating owner profit. Use a contract-level register containing employer, producer, compensation source, earning condition, service period, cancellation right, and offset clause. ERISA section 408(b)(2)(B), codified at 29 U.S.C. 1108(b)(2)(B), requires covered group-health brokerage and consulting arrangements to disclose specified compensation information when the statutory conditions apply. Show indirect commissions alongside employer-paid PEPM charges, including any contractual credits that prevent charging twice for the same promised service.

Translate each employer account into delivery capacity before treating it as a repeatable unit. Contractor budgets are $36,000, $120,000, and $168,000, equivalent to $6,000, $8,000, and $8,400 per annual cohort. At an illustrative blended $100 hourly rate, that purchases sixty, eighty, and eighty-four specialist hours per account. A Base assignment might allocate twenty hours to plan and stop-loss analysis, twenty to PBM repricing, twenty to payroll and loss-run correction, and twenty to renewal execution and reporting. Those hours are a scope budget, not permission to perform licensed activities without the required authority. Use Form 5500 Schedule A and applicable Schedule C information for prospect research, then obtain current contracts because filings can lag and are not complete compensation ledgers. Acquisition budgets of $12,000, $50,000, and $70,000 produce cash CAC of $2,000, $3,333.33, and $3,500 per modeled new employer. This assumes the illustrated acquisition spending supports every cohort in the annualized state; a real mixed renewal book needs separate new-sale and retention attribution. Record founder selling hours separately, because cash CAC excludes the opportunity cost of the owner's time and can otherwise make a relationship-driven brokerage appear artificially scalable.

callout.title: Protect the denominator, compensation source, and delivery budget
callout.body: Experienced operators reconcile the contract, enrollment file, and payer statement before debating headline savings. Small definition errors can consume the entire advisory margin.
items: Attach the exact enrolled-employee counting rule to each PEPM schedule, and reconcile retroactive additions and terminations before invoicing.
Compare broker-of-record effective dates with carrier commission statements; maintain a separate aging queue for incumbent-broker compensation disputes.
Obtain the PBM's rebate eligibility, formulary, specialty, and reconciliation definitions before using NADAC as a comparison benchmark.
Price NCCI correction work by policy year and evidence burden; collect payroll records and revised loss documentation before promising a recovery timetable.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile every deduction from gross entitlements to owner profit
paragraphs: Build the waterfall with deductions that have distinct accounting meanings. External producer allocations reduce the gross entitlement bridge; cancellation, eligibility, and recovery adjustments reduce expected consideration; delivery labor and acquisition spending are operating expenses. In Conservative, $150,000 less $24,000 and $6,000 produces $120,000 revenue. Subtract $36,000 contractor labor, $12,000 acquisition, $9,600 tools, $12,000 licensing, insurance and legal support, and $12,000 general overhead. Owner profit is $38,400, exactly 32%. Base starts with $650,000, subtracts $91,000 and $24,000, and recognizes $535,000. Expenses of $120,000 labor, $50,000 acquisition, $24,000 tools, $35,000 licensing, insurance and legal support, and $65,250 overhead total $294,250. The remaining $240,750 equals 45.0%. Scaled recognizes $950,000 after $158,000 allocations and $42,000 allowances against $1,150,000 entitlements. Its $399,000 expense stack leaves $551,000, exactly 58%. These bridges preserve the supplied scorecard outputs; the detailed expense allocations are explicit modeling assumptions. Never describe the spread between an employer's prior drug expenditure and replacement expenditure as brokerage revenue unless a contract earns that amount for the operator.

Treat owner profit as the modeled residual before owner-level income taxes, distributions, and a separate replacement salary for the working owner. The one full-time person in Conservative and Base is the owner; Scaled includes the owner plus one employee budgeted at $72,000 annual loaded payroll. Three contractors support the first two cases and four support Scaled; those headcounts do not mean full-time-equivalent contractor commitments. Scaled additionally spends $168,000 on contractors, $70,000 on acquisition, $28,000 on tools, $32,000 on licensing, insurance and legal support, and $29,000 on general overhead. The Base overhead allocation is deliberately larger because implementation support, outside bookkeeping, travel, and workflow redesign can be concentrated before scale. This is a reconciliation assumption requiring vendor quotes, not an asserted universal cost curve. Delivery-only contribution equals revenue less contractors: $84,000, $415,000, and $782,000. It is not owner profit and excludes selling, systems, payroll, and overhead. QuickBooks Online can hold account classes while a controlled spreadsheet or SQLite ledger tracks source statements, invoice revisions, service dates, and contractor purchase orders. Never shift implementation work into unpaid founder effort simply to reproduce the target margin.

Scrub expected consideration at the transaction level rather than parking every uncertainty inside one unexplained reserve. Stop-loss commissions can reverse after cancellation, rescission, premium adjustment, or an effective-date dispute. PBM recoveries can shrink when duplicate claims, reversals, excluded specialty products, rebate timing, or guarantee offsets are reconciled. Workers' Comp estimates can disappear when corrected classifications or loss values fail to change the applicable experience modification or when policy-specific premium adjustments offset the benefit. Use gross-entitlement allowance rates of 4.00%, 3.69%, and 3.65% for these illustrative bridges, while recording the actual $6,000, $24,000, and $42,000 amounts exactly. Those percentages are assumptions, not industry loss statistics. Evaluate variable consideration using the contractual earning condition and available evidence; an unresolved success fee may require complete exclusion rather than a modest haircut. Credit losses on an otherwise earned receivable are a different assessment and must not be mislabeled as service reversals. Each month, compare beginning allowance, new estimates, realized adjustments, releases, and ending allowance by payer and cohort. If an adjustment was already reflected in net revenue, its settlement consumes the associated receivable or liability rather than creating a second identical expense.

sections.heading: 3. Fund the collection gap without touching employer claim money
paragraphs: Cash timing starts when delivery spending becomes unavoidable, not when the sales team marks an account won. For a deliberately conservative liquidity screen, assume payout locks of thirty, forty-five, and sixty days, followed by collection periods of sixty, seventy-five, and ninety days for Conservative, Base, and Scaled. Here DSO is measured after release of the lock, so combined gaps are ninety, 120, and 150 days. If a payer's reported DSO already starts at service delivery, adding the lock again would double count the delay. Uniform timing across every revenue stream is a stress simplification; actual PEPM fees, carrier commissions, and recovery splits require separate schedules. Divide annual operating expenses by twelve to obtain monthly cash spending of $6,800, $24,520.83, and $33,250. Using unrounded amounts and thirty-day planning months, expense coverage for those gaps is $20,400, $98,083.33, and $166,250. This estimates a no-receipts runway against the modeled expense base, not a balance-sheet forecast of accounts receivable. A weekly thirteen-week cash projection must replace it before committing to hiring, because annual averages conceal contractor deposits, concentrated renewals, and legal invoices that arrive before the corresponding employer payment.

Add a separate liquidity cushion of $6,000, $24,000, and $42,000 for refunds, offsets, or temporarily disputed collections. The resulting funding envelopes are $26,400, $122,083.33, and $208,250. Matching the allowance amounts is an explicit stress choice, not an accounting requirement: a contra-revenue estimate does not automatically create an equal cash liability. Where the reversal merely cancels an uncollected invoice, model the lost receipt rather than a cash refund; where prior cash must be returned, schedule the payment. The $8,000-$45,000 startup range can support a narrow launch but does not fund the illustrated Base or Scaled collection gap. Likewise, the stated $2,000-$11,000 monthly operating range should not be mistaken for the all-in expense run rate used here, which includes delivery labor, acquisition, and payroll. Reconcile the vendor-specific fixed-cost budget separately rather than forcing these different scopes to match. Use owner capital, retained earnings, or a documented business credit facility for operator liquidity. Employer claim accounts, premium remittances, and plan assets are outside that pool. The prohibited-transaction framework in 29 U.S.C. 1106 makes using plan assets for the operator's convenience a substantive fiduciary issue, not merely a bookkeeping classification error.

Shorten the gap through contract design that matches a real delivered service. Invoice PEPM work monthly in advance where agreed, bill implementation milestones when the corresponding deliverables are accepted, and collect recovery fees only under the negotiated earning and payment terms. Do not relabel an unearned success fee as an implementation charge. A Base employer with $24,000 annual advisory revenue provides $2,000 monthly receipts; that predictable stream can fund specialist work while commissions await carrier processing. Maintain a payer calendar showing service completion, invoice eligibility, statement close, dispute deadline, cash release, and expected bank receipt. Stop-loss specific and aggregate attachment points, lasers, reimbursement conditions, and run-out provisions belong in the employer's risk analysis; the employer's potential shock claim does not become brokerage revenue or brokerage working capital. However, a deficient placement can create professional liability, nonpayment, or lost renewals for the operator. Track those exposures separately from routine DSO. Before using receivables financing, confirm assignment rights, recourse, disputed-invoice exclusions, and offsets; then charge interest and facility fees against the model. Those financing expenses are not included in the canonical bridge, so borrowing without an offsetting cost reduction lowers the stated owner profit.

sections.heading: 4. Stress collectible savings, specialty-drug pathways, and renewal concentration
paragraphs: Apply downside tests to recognized operator revenue, not the employer's total benefit spending. A 10% retained-revenue haircut with expenses unchanged reduces owner profit to $26,400, $187,250, and $456,000. A standalone 20% increase in contractor rates reduces it to $31,200, $216,750, and $517,400. Combining both changes produces $19,200, $163,250, and $422,400. These are sensitivities around the canonical cases, not replacements for them. Losing one equal-sized cohort without immediate expense relief leaves $18,400, $205,083.33, and $503,500. Equal sizing is an analytical convenience; the largest actual employer and shared renewal month are more useful concentration measures. Delivery-only CAC payback, calculated as acquisition spending divided by monthly revenue less contractors, is approximately 1.71, 1.45, and 1.07 months after recurring contribution begins. Add collection timing when evaluating cash recovery, and add the actual sales cycle without double counting overlapping periods. The two-to-five-month first-deal range therefore cannot be treated as a promise of positive cash flow. Require a payer-level downside case that also removes disputed PBM rebates, delays a carrier commission cycle, and replaces an incumbent-defended renewal with a later effective date.

The mapped play erisa_self_funded_specialty_drug_importation_arbitrage, designated TRACK_1, targets self-funded employers with 100-5,000 employees and proposes cross-border specialty-drug savings. Its quoted comparison uses $6,000-$15,000 monthly US PBM list prices against $800-$2,200 foreign prices, with a 25%-35% operator share of claimed annual savings. Test a narrow example: $8,000 minus $1,500 monthly equals $78,000 annually, and 30% would yield $23,400 before delivery and risk deductions. This arithmetic does not establish lawful availability, clinical equivalence, or collectible savings. ERISA status creates no general exemption from federal drug-import restrictions. Under 21 U.S.C. 381 and 384 and 21 CFR Part 251, the available importation framework has specific authorization and product limitations; biological products are excluded from the section 804 eligible-drug definition. A licensed pharmacy in Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand is not sufficient authorization for an employer sourcing program. FDA personal-importation enforcement discretion is not a dependable commercial distribution pathway. Verify the exact product and authorized supply chain before contracting, and assign zero committed revenue to an unqualified pathway. Maintain domestic bridge fills while pursuing eligible domestic purchasing or manufacturer assistance options.

Replace list-price comparisons with adjudicated net cost, including rebates, dispensing charges, shipping, administration, bridge fills, and any employer-funded copay waiver. If the lawful alternative costs $18,000 annually, bridge fills add $6,000, and administration adds $3,000 against a verified $96,000 baseline, net savings are $69,000. A 30% fee is $20,700; a further $2,700 operator delivery cost leaves $18,000 before shared overhead. These are a separate hypothetical example, not incremental revenue inside the canonical scenarios. Patient assistance depends on manufacturer and patient eligibility and cannot be assumed for every commercially insured participant. Begin with independent TPAs and transparent pass-through PBMs, require clinical continuity, and retain domestic fulfillment when eligibility or supply fails. Across the volume's 11 mapped plays, use the same evidence standard without inventing missing play identifiers: compensation must follow an enforceable service and measurable benefit. For Workers' Comp, a lower projected NCCI experience modification does not itself prove a refundable premium; obtain the carrier's policy-year adjustment. For PBM recoveries, reconcile guarantee offsets before charging a split. Protect identifiable claims through applicable HIPAA business-associate arrangements and minimum-necessary access rather than circulating patient-level spreadsheets through prospecting tools.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you allocate startup capital ($8,000–$45,000 USD) and configure a lean, low-opex ($2,000–$11,000 USD/mo) production stack without wasting cash on bloated overhead?
chapters.title: Startup Capital, Lean Infrastructure & Pre-Flight Stack
chapters.subtitle: Reserve-First Capital, ERISA Compensation Controls, HIPAA-Scoped Infrastructure, and 340B Split-Billing Economics
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40, ranked #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, turns benefits administration complexity into retained advisory and recovery fees. Across 11 mapped plays, the capital constraint is collection timing, not software breadth. Allocate $8,000–$45,000 with at least half protected as working capital, then purchase licensed execution, insurance, secure records, and narrowly scoped automation. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled; employer premiums, claim funds, and pharmacy reimbursements are excluded from operator revenue. This chapter specifies twelve infrastructure layers, reconciles fixed overhead against total scenario costs, and separates a lean advisory launch from capital-intensive pharmacy ownership. Release spending only against verified authority, signed economics, tested access controls, and a documented path from completed work to collected cash.

sections.heading: 1. Protect the reserve before buying production capacity
paragraphs: Allocate startup money around the two-to-five-month first-deal window, not around a software shopping list. The three capital envelopes below are purchase limits, not vendor quotations or additional revenue scenarios. An $8,000 launch places $4,000 in reserve and spends $4,000 establishing a narrow advisory operation; the $25,000 envelope protects $15,000; the $45,000 envelope protects $27,000. Those reserve shares are 50%, 60%, and 60%. Hold the reserve in a separate business deposit account with an insured institution, verify ownership-category coverage, and reconcile transfers weekly. It belongs to the operator and must never contain employer claim money, pharmacy inventory proceeds, or premium remittances. At $2,000 monthly fixed overhead, the smallest reserve buys only two months before collections. A five-month delay requires $10,000 of fixed-cost coverage, leaving a $6,000 reserve shortfall in that envelope. Resolve the shortfall through additional committed owner liquidity, a smaller operating scope, or legitimately earned advance advisory fees with explicit deliverables. Do not bridge it by borrowing from a client's benefit account. Treat the $8,000 entry point as conditional on existing credentials and a short sales cycle, rather than sufficient funding for every jurisdiction or service line.

Reconcile overhead to Formula v2.0 before selecting a staffing plan. Conservative retained revenue of $120,000 less $38,400 owner profit implies $81,600 total annual costs. Base revenue of $535,000 less $240,750 implies $294,250; Scaled revenue of $950,000 less $551,000 implies $399,000. These totals produce the required 32%, 45.0%, and 58% margins without changing the supplied revenue basis. For planning, assign fixed monthly operating envelopes of $2,000, $6,000, and $11,000 respectively. Their annual totals are $24,000, $72,000, and $132,000, leaving $57,600, $222,250, and $267,000 for all remaining scenario expenses. Those residuals must absorb contractor delivery, payroll where applicable, acquisition costs, transaction charges, and other modeled expenses; they are not extra owner distributions. The team remains one full-time operator plus three contractors in Conservative and Base, then two full-time staff plus four contractors in Scaled. Contractor counts describe available specialists, not three guaranteed full-time retainers. Fund work orders against signed assignments and measured collection cycles. Do not subtract a fresh assumed owner salary from the published profit and still label the result the canonical scorecard. Track any alternate compensation presentation separately, with its bridge to these exact totals.

Translate sales assumptions into collectible units before releasing discretionary cash. An illustrative account with 250 enrolled employees paying a retained $8 PEPM produces $2,000 monthly operator revenue and $24,000 over twelve fully billable months. Five such full-year accounts produce the Conservative $120,000 revenue figure, but five accounts signed late in the year do not. Apply the actual contract definition of eligible or enrolled lives, effective dates, and billing cutoffs. For recovery work, a documented $40,000 workers' compensation premium refund at a 25% contractual split produces $10,000 operator revenue after the agreed collection trigger, not $40,000. Exclude disputed estimates until the applicable recognition criteria are met. A 13-week cash schedule should distinguish earned fees, invoices, carrier commission statements, bank receipts, and refundable advances. Release outreach spending in weekly increments rather than annual lead-platform contracts. Keep commission reversals and contingent-fee disputes visible as reserve demands. At the upper $11,000 fixed-overhead setting, $27,000 covers only about 2.45 months; holding five months requires a fixed burn no greater than $5,400 unless additional liquidity exists. Buy the next capacity layer only when collected contribution supports it, not because pipeline premiums look impressive on a presentation.

callout.title: Buy collection certainty before buying more leads
callout.body: Experienced operators protect the reserve by narrowing deliverables, controlling release conditions, and purchasing specialist time only when needed.
items: Obtain carrier commission schedules and reversal terms before presenting PEPM-plus-commission economics; disclose both streams and model their different collection dates.

sections.heading: 2. Assemble twelve layers without creating twelve data silos
paragraphs: Build one identity boundary, one controlled document repository, and one auditable calculation path. The twelve-layer matrix provides exact reference pricing assumptions for named tiers, not verified current offers; confirm checkout prices, minimum seats, regional charges, and contractual terms before committing. Annual-billing rates are monthly equivalents and can create upfront cash requirements. Microsoft 365 Business Premium at the $22 reference rate buys the primary productivity and endpoint-control layer; Bitwarden Teams at $4 supplies shared secrets without spreadsheets. Two seats of each produce $52 monthly before tax at these assumptions. HubSpot Free receives employer contacts and renewal dates, never member claims. Calendly Standard receives meeting logistics, not diagnoses. Adobe Acrobat Standard handles redacted proposals and document preparation; its listed price does not purchase a specialized health-record workflow. PostgreSQL, Python, and Metabase provide a reproducible calculation stack without per-claim software fees. Open-source licensing does not eliminate patching, database administration, backups, or contractor expense. Keep source-control repositories free of claim extracts, production credentials, and live employer census files. Purchase commercial seats for actual operators rather than every occasional reviewer, and explicitly verify whether a contractor's access is permitted by the selected license.

Treat protected health information as a separate deployment decision. A vendor's brand, encryption claim, or enterprise marketing page does not establish that a particular service and configuration can receive it. Map each disclosure to the plan, covered entity, business associate, or other applicable role; execute required business associate agreements and document minimum-necessary access before loading identifiable claims. Microsoft services require confirmation of the applicable agreement and service scope. AWS requires an executed agreement and eligible services configured according to the assigned responsibilities. The EC2 and S3 rates below omit storage attachments, keys, requests, transfer, monitoring, and recovery copies; the compute reference is not an all-in production quote. Bind PostgreSQL to private connectivity, encrypt volumes and backups, disable public buckets, and use short-lived application credentials. Require phishing-resistant multifactor authentication for privileged users, separate administrator accounts from daily mail accounts, and remove contractor access at assignment closure. Synthetic claims should populate development environments. A limited data set remains regulated information under HIPAA and is not interchangeable with properly de-identified data. If the necessary contracts or controls cannot be established economically, leave claims with the authorized administrator and accept aggregate outputs sufficient for the contracted analysis.

Automate calculations only after documenting their inputs and exceptions. Use Department of Labor EFAST2 public filings for prospect research, record the filing year, and distinguish Schedule A insurance information from Schedule C service-provider reporting; neither schedule is a complete current renewal calendar. Confirm renewal dates directly before outreach. For PBM analysis, import CMS NADAC reference files with effective dates, normalize NDC representations, and compare equivalent package quantities. NADAC is an acquisition-cost benchmark, not a specialty reimbursement promise or a complete measure of net plan cost. Reconcile dispensing fees, rebates, member cost sharing, exclusions, and invoice timing separately. For workers' compensation, ingest authorized payroll registers, class-code assignments, loss runs, and the applicable experience-rating worksheet. NCCI rules apply only where relevant; independent bureaus and jurisdiction-specific filing practices require different adapters. Store each source version and transformation checksum with the output. Run a known-case regression suite before updating any pricing file or rating assumption. An analyst should be able to reproduce an employer's invoice from frozen inputs without opening a private chat thread. If records disagree, suspend the affected savings assertion and route the discrepancy to the carrier, administrator, or pharmacy partner instead of silently substituting a favorable number.
