sections.heading: 3. Separate entity authority, client money, and pharmacy economics
paragraphs: Establish the operating entity, tax identifier, bank accounts, bookkeeping categories, and written signing authority before binding engagements. Verify individual and business-entity producer requirements in every relevant state, including Life and Health authority for benefits work and Property and Casualty authority for workers' compensation brokerage. Carrier appointments, referral restrictions, consultant rules, and TPA licensing depend on the actual activity; holding one producer license does not authorize all administrative services. California Insurance Code section 1631 illustrates the prohibition on unlicensed insurance solicitation and negotiation, but the operating checklist must follow the client's jurisdictions. Purchase professional liability and cyber coverage for the stated services, check exclusions for pharmacy operations and benefit-plan fiduciary acts, and obtain subcontractor coverage evidence. Record commissions and retained advisory fees in separate ledger categories. Do not route employer premiums or claim payments through the ordinary operating account. Where handling such money is unavoidable and authorized, implement the applicable separate-account and reconciliation requirements first. For covered group-health brokerage or consulting arrangements expecting at least $1,000 in compensation, build the ERISA section 408(b)(2)(B) disclosure process around services, direct and indirect compensation, payer relationships, and timing before entering, extending, or renewing the arrangement. Maintain evidence of delivery to the responsible fiduciary.

The mapped play section_340b_contract_pharmacy_spread_arbitrage requires a separate contracting lane, not a casual extension of employer benefits brokerage. Partner only with an eligible, registered covered entity, such as a qualifying Federally Qualified Health Center, Ryan White provider, or eligible hospital category; rural location alone does not establish eligibility. Section 340B, codified at 42 U.S.C. 256b, governs ceiling prices, duplicate discounts, diversion, and covered-entity obligations. A modeled 25–50% acquisition discount must be validated by actual eligible-drug invoices; it is not a universal statutory percentage. Commercial reimbursement depends on the payer contract and adjudicated claim, rather than an entitlement to collect an assumed full price. For a deliberately simplified eligible prescription, $10,000 collected reimbursement minus $6,000 acquisition cost, $400 pharmacy fulfillment expense, and a $250 operator administrative fee leaves $3,350 with the covered entity before its other expenses. The operator recognizes only its $250 fee; $150 of attributable delivery expense leaves $100 contribution before shared overhead. One hundred comparable completed prescriptions would yield $25,000 operator revenue and $10,000 contribution, not $1 million of operator revenue. This sensitivity example does not supplement or replace the three canonical annual cases.

Design flat administrative or dispensing compensation around documented services and supportable market value; the word flat does not resolve referral incentives or federal Anti-Kickback Statute exposure. Assess 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b), applicable state restrictions, payer contracts, and the real patient-care relationship before accepting tele-referral or specialty capture arrangements. Require encounter evidence, prescription linkage, prescriber attribution, Medicaid duplicate-discount controls, reversal handling, and auditable accumulator logic. A telehealth encounter alone does not establish 340B patient eligibility. The covered entity retains oversight even when a vendor performs split billing. If contract-pharmacy restrictions block an NDC, assess a genuinely entity-owned specialty pharmacy alongside contract pharmacies, with separate licensing, payer enrollment, staffing, inventory, and capital underwriting. That ownership fallback is outside this chapter's $8,000–$45,000 advisory launch envelope. Automate 340B ESP uploads only when applicable manufacturer terms, lawful disclosure authority, contractual permissions, and data minimization support them; submission alone does not ensure access to restricted products. Reconcile uploaded records to claims and inventory without transmitting unnecessary identifiers. If an eligible dispensing pathway remains unavailable, suspend that product's capture and continue the ordinary benefits advisory business. Never convert an unresolved eligibility question into projected spread revenue merely to justify the software purchase.

sections.heading: 4. Prove readiness with one complete transaction before scaling
paragraphs: Run pre-launch readiness as a series of evidence tests, not a collection of purchased subscriptions. Start with one consenting employer, one defined service, one authorized data source, and one signed compensation schedule. For a self-funded transition, the case file must identify current plan terms, proposed specific and aggregate stop-loss attachment points, exclusions, lasers, contract basis, run-out obligations, and funding responsibilities. An attractive premium comparison does not settle shock-claim liquidity or coverage gaps between policies. Record who evaluates reference-based pricing balance-bill exposure and who provides any contracted legal defense; do not imply that a repricing algorithm supplies representation. For a PBM review, obtain rebate definitions, reconciliation timing, audit rights, exclusions, and guarantees from executed contracts. For an E-Mod assignment, confirm the bureau, experience period, payroll classifications, correction procedures, and carrier refund process. A projected modifier change is not a received refund. Build the invoice from the resulting authorized service evidence and reconcile it to the contractual trigger. If the first deal cannot be explained from source document through calculation to bank receipt, more prospect volume will multiply exceptions rather than improve the operating model. Keep that first transaction small enough to review completely.

Test controls using synthetic cases before any live claim import. Include a duplicate prescription, a reversed claim, a mismatched NDC package, an ineligible encounter, a missing payroll classification, and a stale loss valuation. The expected behavior is an exception record with an assigned owner, not a silently completed savings calculation. Restore a backup into an isolated environment and prove that document versions, calculation inputs, access permissions, and invoice evidence remain usable. Test contractor offboarding by removing access and checking active sessions, shared links, service tokens, and local synchronization. Maintain an incident contact sheet covering the customer, insurer, hosting provider, and specialist response support. HIPAA security requirements at 45 CFR 164.308 include risk analysis, workforce controls, contingency planning, and evaluation where applicable; 45 CFR 164.502(e) addresses business-associate arrangements. Translate each applicable requirement into an owner and retained evidence. Do not send production claim files through ordinary scheduling or prospect automation accounts. Use an access review to verify that aggregate dashboards cannot expose underlying member rows through exports or drill-through features. A successful screenshot is insufficient when the actual export path remains unrestricted or the recovery copy cannot be restored.

Release additional capacity only after reconciling delivery economics and cash timing for the completed pilot. Track enrolled lives actually invoiced, retained PEPM, commission receipts, contractor hours, correction cycles, refunds collected, and days from completed work to cash. Maintain a separate register for employer savings estimates so they cannot inflate operator revenue. For principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606, document which services the operator controls and which receipts merely pass through; the supplied scorecard uses retained operator revenue and excludes premiums and claim funds. Do not apply a second retained-share haircut to amounts already supplied on that basis. Review the 13-week forecast every week and compare actual spending with the fixed-overhead envelope plus remaining scenario costs. At $535,000 Base revenue, allowing annual costs above $294,250 necessarily reduces the stated $240,750 profit unless revenue also changes. Preserve that arithmetic when considering another contractor or application. Expand one dimension at a time: more employers, another jurisdiction, or another service line. If collection slows, freeze discretionary acquisition, renegotiate delivery timing, and return to the lowest-cost validated workflow. Scaling should purchase measured throughput while preserving source traceability, not conceal unresolved exceptions behind a larger team.

callout.title: Four proofs required before the first live production file
callout.body: The principal retains the evidence and assigns a named owner to every unresolved exception; a purchased subscription is not evidence of readiness.
items: Authority proof: verify applicable producer and entity authority, appointments, TPA scope, signed engagement terms, and required compensation disclosures.

chapters.question_prompt: What kills 80% of newcomers in self-funded health, pbm & workers' comp arbitrage, and what forensic metrics detect margin leaks, regulatory landmines, or platform bans before they wipe out capital?
chapters.title: Beginner Traps, Clawbacks & Asymmetric Failure Modes
chapters.subtitle: Stop-Loss Lasers, PBM Rebate Receivables, NCCI Corrections, ERISA Compensation Disclosures, and WOTC Evidence Controls
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40, Rank #08 of 42, scores 93/100, but its eleven mapped plays depend on disciplined evidence, contract boundaries, and collectible compensation. This chapter tests renewal intelligence, benefits advisory, self-funding transitions, captive placement, stop-loss placement, TPA selection, PBM repricing, rebate recovery, reference-based pricing, E-Mod recovery, and the WOTC/Section 41 engine against asymmetric failure. Annual owner profit remains $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled; employer claim funds and insurance premiums never become operator revenue. The question's 80% framing is not a measured failure rate. The practical objective is to detect missing coverage, disputed rebates, invalid classifications, unsupported tax claims, access suspensions, and commission reversals before an attractive spreadsheet becomes an unfunded obligation.

sections.heading: 1. Refuse the Coverage Gap Before Selling the Savings
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is treating an employer's premium budget as the brokerage's addressable revenue. A $4 million health-plan budget is an employer funding obligation, not $4 million of agency sales. Renewal intelligence from EFAST2 Form 5500 filings identifies potential conversations, but Schedule A and Schedule C are neither universal nor current contract inventories. A self-funded arrangement can have incomplete commission visibility in those schedules, and filing exemptions remove some prospects entirely. Confirm plan funding, renewal date, incumbent authority, and actual decision rights directly. For benefits advisory, 1,000 covered employees at $8 PEPM produces $96,000 annually only if the agreement bills employees rather than members and all twelve months remain collectible. A covered-life count of 1,800 does not justify billing 1,800 employees. Build a monthly census bridge covering additions, terminations, retroactive eligibility changes, and invoice adjustments. Stop automated invoicing when unexplained census differences exceed 1%; that is an internal investigation threshold, not an industry standard. Incumbent broker defense typically attacks timing, compensation ambiguity, and coverage continuity. Counter with signed authority and reconciled facts, never fabricated incumbent fees or unsupported savings claims. The safe fallback is a fixed-scope diagnostic while the incumbent coverage remains intact.

The second and third traps are buying a stop-loss headline and forgetting the calendar. A $100,000 specific attachment point does not protect a claimant carrying a $500,000 individual laser. If that claimant incurs $420,000 of otherwise eligible expenses, employer exposure can be $420,000 rather than $100,000, a $320,000 difference before other policy terms. An aggregate attachment is not automatically a second route around that exclusion; inspect how laser claims enter the aggregate calculation. Compare incurred and paid windows, terminal liability, actively-at-work language, disclosure duties, reimbursement deadlines, and advance-funding provisions against the plan document and TPA agreement. A 12/12 arrangement and a 12/15 arrangement allocate late-paid claims differently. Never describe a three-month extension as complete protection against every late submission. For self-funding transitions and stop-loss placement, require a claimant-specific exposure schedule and a monthly cash stress test. A $250,000 eligible claim reimbursed sixty days later still requires $250,000 of interim liquidity unless an enforceable advance mechanism applies. Pause placement when any material claimant falls outside the signed coverage comparison. The fallback is to retain existing coverage or select a fully insured alternative rather than finance the employer's shock claim from the operator's working capital.

The fourth trap is presenting captive participation as premium savings without contingent liabilities. A $75,000 contribution plus a possible $50,000 assessment creates a different exposure from a fixed $75,000 premium; collateral, exit accounting, and loss-development provisions determine the actual commitment. The fifth trap is outsourcing TPA selection to a commission grid. Reconcile eligibility feeds, claim-payment authority, stop-loss reporting, banking controls, and termination assistance before comparing administrative prices. A $2 PEPM discount across 1,000 employees saves $24,000 annually, but one unrecoverable $60,000 reporting defect overwhelms it. The sixth trap is selling reference-based pricing as a discount that providers must accept. If an illustrative $100,000 billed service yields a $30,000 plan payment and a $20,000 negotiated settlement, the relevant employer cost is $50,000 plus defense and administration, not the initial payment alone. Confirm provider agreements, participant communications, appeals, balance-bill defense, and federal surprise-billing rules where applicable. Escalate every collection notice immediately rather than waiting for a monthly dashboard. State producer authority and any required TPA authority must match the actual activities. When defense capacity or licensing is missing, use properly authorized partners and narrower services; do not convert an advice engagement into unauthorized claims administration or custody.

sections.heading: 2. Rebuild PBM Savings from Adjudicated Claims and Collectible Rebates
paragraphs: The seventh trap is repricing pharmacy claims against NADAC and calling the difference recoverable spread. NADAC is a survey-based acquisition-cost reference, not the employer's contract price or a universal benchmark for specialty, limited-distribution, or unavailable products. Normalize NDC format, package quantity, dispensing units, service dates, reversals, ingredient cost, dispensing fees, and member cost share before comparing transactions. Suppose 10,000 comparable paid prescriptions show $1,200,000 in employer and member payments against a $1,050,000 modeled alternative. The $150,000 difference is a screening result, not operator revenue and not automatically an enforceable refund. If implementation and network effects cost $40,000, estimated employer improvement falls to $110,000. A separately contracted 20% fee would equal $22,000 only on the agreed, validated measurement basis. Stop the repricing run when unmatched product or unit records exceed 2% of evaluated spend; inspect all high-dollar exceptions even below that threshold. Compare therapeutic and network disruption before promising savings. The fallback is a paid procurement comparison with clearly separated measured, modeled, and excluded populations, not a recovery demand built from unmatched benchmarks. Preserve the original extract and transformation log so a challenger can reproduce every included claim without receiving unnecessary patient identifiers.

The eighth trap is equating a pass-through label with ownership of every manufacturer dollar. Rebate definitions may exclude administrative fees, purchase discounts, price-protection payments, specialty arrangements, or amounts earned through affiliated entities. Read the economic definition, permitted deductions, reconciliation timing, audit rights, termination tail, and disputes process. At 1,000 eligible members, a $300 annual guarantee suggests $300,000, but a contract excluding 200 members from that guarantee produces $240,000 before other adjustments. A 15% recovery fee on a verified $60,000 incremental payment is $9,000; it is not 15% of all historical rebates. Establish one ledger for amounts contractually earned, another for invoiced receivables, and another for cash received. Flag an unpaid amount immediately after its contractual due date and suspend any discretionary distributions tied to that receivable. A rebate payable 180 days after quarter-end is not late at day ninety, although it still creates a working-capital requirement. Tie contingency recognition to the accountant-approved treatment of variable consideration and reversal risk. If the PBM refuses the evidence needed to establish an amount, pursue contractual audit or dispute channels and revert to an agreed fixed-fee analytical scope. Do not invent an accrual to preserve a monthly sales target.

The ninth trap combines hidden remuneration with careless health-information access. ERISA Section 408(b)(2)(B), codified at 29 U.S.C. 1108(b)(2)(B), imposes disclosure requirements on covered group-health brokerage and consulting arrangements expecting at least $1,000 in direct or indirect compensation. Disclose applicable commissions, referral compensation, and payment formulas; merely saying that carriers may pay compensation does not explain a known arrangement. Whether a particular person is a fiduciary depends on their functions, not their business card. Separate compensation analysis from claim-level processing permissions. Execute required business associate arrangements when performing covered functions involving protected health information, apply minimum-necessary access where required, and restrict employer access according to plan-administration rules. A pharmacy extract containing 40,000 rows does not justify forty thousand patient names in a sales workspace. Use purpose-limited identifiers and secure transfers, with named accounts and access expiration. Stop processing upon an authorization mismatch, a rejected credential, or an export outside the agreed purpose. Do not bypass a portal suspension with shared credentials, rotating accounts, or scraped session tokens. Those shortcuts can terminate contractual access and create additional liability. Preserve the failure evidence, contact the authorized administrator, and use an approved export while permissions are repaired.

callout.title: Four Veteran Habits That Protect the Recovery
callout.body: The valuable artifact is a reproducible entitlement calculation backed by enforceable terms, not a spectacular savings percentage.
items: Freeze the pre-renewal PBM extract and record its checksum before cleaning; retain a separate reversal and unit-conversion exception ledger.
Ask stop-loss underwriters to identify every claimant-specific deviation in the final quotation and reconcile it again against issued endorsements.
Track PBM termination-tail rebates by earned quarter, contractual payment date, audit deadline, and the party entitled to collect.
Submit E-Mod correction packets with original unit statistical records, supporting payroll records, and a before-and-after calculation that preserves unrelated adjustments.

sections.heading: 3. Separate Bureau Corrections from Tax Credits and Unsupported Recoveries
paragraphs: The tenth trap is changing workers' compensation classifications because a cheaper code appears plausible. Actual operations, governing classification rules, state exceptions, payroll segregation, and supporting records control the result. NCCI does not administer every jurisdiction; California uses WCIRB, and other states have independent arrangements. Obtain the applicable bureau worksheet, policy audits, payroll detail, and carrier unit statistical reporting. A simple illustration uses $300,000 of mod-sensitive premium: changing the modifier from 1.20 to 1.10 suggests a $30,000 difference before other rating factors. At a permitted 25% recovery share, the operator fee is $7,500 only if the defined recovery is actually supported and the agreement's earning conditions are met. Do not apply that percentage to total payroll, claim reserves, or the entire premium invoice. Expense constants, discounts, state assessments, and policy-specific adjustments can change the final refund. Stop the demand whenever the governing classification or reporting period is unresolved. The fallback is a fixed-fee payroll and classification review with an appropriately licensed producer handling placement or premium negotiations. Never coach an employer to relabel hazardous work, conceal subcontractors, or alter time records; those actions create false applications rather than legitimate rating corrections.

The eleventh trap is assuming a closed claim automatically repairs an experience modifier. Rating uses defined experience periods, valuation dates, loss limitations, and reporting procedures. A $100,000 reserve reduction after a valuation date may affect a later calculation, an allowable revision, or neither immediate premium nor the current worksheet. Trace each proposed adjustment from carrier claim history through unit statistical reporting to the bureau's applicable revision rules. Track correction acceptance separately from refund issuance and client receipt. Flag a carrier acknowledgment missing after ten business days as an internal service escalation, while respecting the actual contractual and bureau deadlines. The twelfth trap is ignoring commission chargebacks when a corrected premium falls or a policy cancels. If a $20,000 commission has a contractually determined $6,000 reversal, available contribution falls by $6,000 even though the sales report still celebrates the placement. Maintain a policy-level chargeback schedule covering earning rules, cancellation provisions, audits, and producer splits. For recovery compensation, confirm state restrictions and avoid promising advocacy beyond the operator's authority. If a carrier disputes causation or timing, preserve the written decision and invoke the applicable review process. Do not net a disputed recovery against employer premiums or withhold claim funds to force payment.

The mapped play wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine combines authorized WOTC screening with separately substantiated Section 41 work; it does not make employee hiring a research activity. Verify statutory program authorization for each hiring date before projecting WOTC. Do not assume a post-2025 start date qualifies merely because payroll software offers a screening form. For an authorized hiring period, complete Form 8850 pre-screening as required and submit the certification request to the designated state workforce agency within the applicable 28-day deadline. In an illustration involving ten certified employees in a qualifying category with a $6,000 wage limit, each reaching 400 hours and sufficient eligible wages, the 40% rate yields $2,400 each, or $24,000. A hypothetical permitted 15% service fee is $3,600, never $24,000 of operator revenue. Wage coordination can reduce the credit; maintain an employee-level allocation ledger. Section 41 requires its own activity analysis, qualified-expense support, funded-research review, and applicable base calculation. A separately validated $50,000 credit could imply a $5,000 fee at 10% only where professional and other applicable fee rules permit. Exclude unsupported claims and use fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review when eligibility or fee authority fails.

sections.heading: 4. Install Cash, Access, and Evidence Circuit Breakers Before Scaling
paragraphs: Keep the canonical Formula v2.0 cases separate from every downside illustration. Conservative recognized operator revenue is $120,000; at 32% net margin, costs are $81,600 and annual owner profit is $38,400. Base revenue is $535,000; at 45.0%, costs are $294,250 and profit is $240,750. Scaled revenue is $950,000; at 58%, costs are $399,000 and profit is $551,000. Staffing stays 1 FT + 3 C for Conservative and Base, and 2 FT + 4 C for Scaled. One illustrative composition, not an additional scorecard assumption, reconciles Conservative as $96,000 PEPM fees plus $18,000 retained commissions plus $6,000 recovery fees. Base can reconcile as 3,000 employees times $10 times twelve months, plus $125,000 commissions and $50,000 recovery fees. Scaled can reconcile as 5,000 employees times $11 times twelve, plus $200,000 commissions and $90,000 recovery fees. These components must already reflect the operator's retained share where applicable; never deduct the same producer split twice. Determine gross-versus-net presentation under ASC 606 from the actual principal-agent relationship, not the scorecard's shorthand revenue label. Employer premiums, pharmacy spend, recovered tax credits, and claim funds stay outside these revenue totals.

The thirteenth trap is running an agency on accrued wins while paying contractors in cash. Track cash collected, revenue recognized, disputed receivables, expected commission reversals, and contractor commitments separately. The stated $2,000–$11,000 monthly operating range is a planning input, not the full expense denominator behind every canonical profit case; do not substitute that range for scorecard costs. At the upper planning level, three months requires $33,000 before claim disputes or owner withdrawals. Startup capital of $8,000–$45,000 and a two-to-five-month first-deal cycle make collection timing material. Use an internal stop on discretionary owner distributions when unrestricted cash falls below three months of committed outflows. Reserve commission exposure using contract-specific earning schedules rather than a convenient flat percentage. A Base downside illustration with $25,000 of lost recognized revenue and $15,000 of additional dispute expense reduces profit from $240,750 to $200,750, assuming other costs remain unchanged. That illustration does not revise the canonical Base case. Investigate receivables thirty days beyond their contractual due date and any client exceeding 25% of annual retained revenue. Concentration is an exposure signal, not an automatic reason to terminate a good client. Renegotiate deposits, milestones, or fixed fees before expanding unfunded work.

The fourteenth trap is automating a broken permission model. Public Form 5500 research, employer claim extracts, PBM portals, and bureau worksheets have different access rights; one employer signature does not authorize every downstream system action. Respect published access methods, service terms, rate limits, and the precise scope of delegated authority. Stop after an authorization rejection or account suspension; repeated evasion attempts can convert a repairable access issue into permanent termination. Detect bulk-export anomalies, new administrator accounts, unexpected destination changes, and expired client authority. For this chapter, the eleven operating lanes are renewal intelligence, benefits advisory, self-funding transitions, captive placement, stop-loss placement, TPA selection, PBM repricing, rebate recovery, reference-based pricing, E-Mod recovery, and the named WOTC/Section 41 engine; these labels organize work rather than assert additional catalog identifiers. Give each lane an evidence owner and a recoverable shutdown procedure. Preserve raw records, calculation versions, signed terms, and correction history under a documented retention schedule. When a defect appears, stop the affected calculation, quantify exposed revenue and client obligations, notify the authorized decision-maker, and resume only after correction is verified. A small team survives by narrowing unsupported work immediately, not by hiding exceptions until renewal.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the affected lane
sop_steps.action: Suspend the disputed calculation, submission, invoice line, or portal session without disabling unrelated authorized work.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve original extracts, timestamps, contract versions, access events, and the current client-facing calculation.

sop_steps.title: Quantify the actual exposure
sop_steps.action: Separate employer obligations, operator retained revenue, repayable commissions, receivables, and incremental correction costs.
sop_steps.detail: Calculate a bounded downside using specific contract terms; never count employer claim funds as available agency liquidity.

sop_steps.title: Assign the authorized correction
sop_steps.action: Route coverage defects to the licensed producer, reporting defects to the carrier or TPA, and tax questions to independent tax review.
sop_steps.detail: Notify the responsible client decision-maker and record applicable response, appeal, filing, and contractual dispute deadlines.

sop_steps.title: Verify before resuming
sop_steps.action: Reperform the affected reconciliation against corrected evidence and obtain the required client or administrator authorization.
sop_steps.detail: Resume only the repaired scope, update reserves and forecasts, and add the defect to the recurring exception checklist.

chapters.pull_quote: A recovery becomes a business only when the evidence survives challenge and the retained fee survives collection.
action_checklist: Build a claimant-level stop-loss comparison covering lasers, incurred and paid windows, reimbursement timing, and employer liquidity.
Reconcile PEPM invoices to the contracted employee denominator and investigate unexplained census differences above 1%.
Version PBM claim transformations and separate modeled spread, enforceable recoveries, rebate receivables, and collected fees.
Tie every E-Mod correction to governing bureau rules, carrier reporting, actual refund mechanics, and commission reversal exposure.
Validate WOTC hiring-date authorization, certification timing, wage coordination, and separate Section 41 support before any claim or outcome-linked fee.
Install cash-runway, overdue-receivable, client-concentration, evidence-completeness, and access-rejection controls with named owners.

chapters.question_prompt: Where do high-margin deals, clients, or undervalued assets hide in self-funded health, pbm & workers' comp arbitrage, and what repeatable outbound/inbound sourcing system lands the first 3-to-10 wins (2–5 months)?
chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: Form 5500 Renewal Signals, SEC EDGAR Executive Triggers, NADAC Repricing, and NCCI E-Mod Recovery Mandates
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40 ranks #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score because employer benefit friction creates several monetizable entry points without owning claim risk. This chapter maps 11 sourcing plays into one evidence-led acquisition system: public filings identify timing, authorized records establish recoverability, and narrowly priced mandates convert interest into retained fees. Target the first 3-to-10 signed wins over 2–5 months using renewal calendars, executive changes, PBM contract mismatches, and workers' compensation corrections. Canonical annual owner profit is $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled. Those outcomes use retained operator revenue, never employer premiums or claim funds. The operating advantage is disciplined qualification, documented compensation, and outreach tied to a verifiable event rather than speculative savings.

key_metrics.context: Annual retained operator revenue; employer premiums and claim funds excluded

sections.heading: 1. Mine renewal windows and executive events before buying broad lead lists
paragraphs: Build the first account universe around employers with roughly 200–2,000 covered employees, an identifiable benefits decision maker, and enough time before renewal to evaluate alternatives. Treat this band as an initial targeting hypothesis, not a universal underwriting threshold. Download Department of Labor Form 5500 datasets through EFAST2 resources; join employer EIN, plan number, filing year, participant counts, and Schedule A contract periods into a dated account record. Separate health contracts from dental, vision, disability, and life coverage before assigning a renewal hypothesis. Schedule A insurance periods do not automatically establish a self-funded medical renewal, and Schedule C reporting is not a complete broker compensation ledger. Public filings can lag operating reality, amended filings can replace earlier values, and exemptions leave some employers outside this universe. Verify timing on the first conversation. An illustrative batch of 120 employers might yield 36 apparently relevant renewal windows and 12 verified dates; these are planning assumptions, not published conversion rates. Store source URL, retrieval date, evidence excerpt, and confidence separately from inferred need. Never turn a participant count into enrolled employees without checking the definition. The first sellable deliverable is a renewal evidence brief, not an unsolicited proposal claiming that a captive or self-funded plan will save money.

Implement sec_edgar_8k_vendor_trigger_arbitrage as a timing layer over that employer universe. Poll SEC EDGAR current-filing RSS feeds and documented JSON endpoints where available; resolve the accession, issuer identity, filing type, and event text rather than relying on keyword headlines. Form D reports exempt offerings, but the amount offered is not cash received; distinguish it from the reported amount sold. Route Form 8-K Item 5.02 departures or appointments, Item 1.01 material agreements, and Item 2.01 acquisition closings into separate queues. None proves benefit dissatisfaction. Require an employer match and a plausible operating consequence, such as acquired workforces or a new CFO inheriting renewal decisions. Use an identifying User-Agent, a token bucket capped at five requests per second across workers, deduplication by accession, and backoff on throttling. Each night, mirror available SEC bulk ZIP archives for historical lookbacks; use daily indexes and accession retrieval where no corresponding ZIP exists. Do not assume every feed has a nightly archive. A batch of 40 events producing eight relevant accounts and two conversations is an explicit test case. Aim for human-reviewed, sub-hour executive outreach after ingestion, before slower commercial databases refresh; measure actual latency rather than promising universal speed.

Map the chapter's 11 sourcing plays to distinct buying reasons: EDGAR executive triggers, Form 5500 renewal targeting, Schedule A/C compensation discovery, acquisition census reconciliation, NADAC benchmark repricing, PBM rebate reconciliation, stop-loss renewal comparison, TPA service unbundling, NCCI E-Mod correction, payroll classification review, and partner-led diagnostic demand. The matrix starts the first seven; the next section completes the map. Keep the outreach consequence specific. A new CFO receives a dated renewal-risk brief; an acquired business receives a census and contract inventory; an employer with a transparent PBM already receives no spread accusation. For compensation discovery, 600 covered employees at $4 PEPM creates $28,800 annual advisory fees only after enrollment, scope, and payment terms are confirmed. An acquisition census engagement priced at 800 employees times $3 PEPM also produces $28,800 annually, but do not stack both fees for identical work. A $500,000 stop-loss premium with a contractual 3% commission produces $15,000 gross commission before any contractual sharing. Neither premium nor alleged employer savings becomes operator revenue. Where evidence is weak, offer a fixed-scope inventory instead of an outcome fee. Preserve a written reason to abandon each play when the incumbent arrangement already meets the employer's needs.

callout.title: Win the timing advantage without manufacturing a savings story
callout.body: Experienced operators sell a verifiable next step while preserving the employer's existing service continuity.
items: Compare amended Form 5500 filings before outreach; a revised Schedule A can invalidate the renewal date in a purchased lead list.
Link every EDGAR event to an actual employer operating unit; investment vehicles and special-purpose issuers often produce irrelevant alerts.
Keep the PBM contract definition beside each rebate calculation; an attractive benchmark cannot override excluded utilization or settlement language.
Ask for the current E-Mod worksheet and state bureau identity first; NCCI procedures do not govern every state's rating system.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify recoverable economics before requesting sensitive records
paragraphs: Use a 100-point qualification scorecard with six explicit components: renewal or correction timing worth 20 points, verified economic exposure worth 25, access to a budget owner worth 15, accessible contract evidence worth 15, licensed delivery capacity worth 15, and workable payment terms worth 10. Define full, partial, and zero credit in the CRM rather than letting enthusiasm determine the score. Full timing credit means a confirmed review window and enough implementation time; a rumored renewal earns five points at most. Economic exposure requires a defensible fee basis after delivery cost, not a large premium alone. Work accounts scoring at least 75 immediately, nurture 60–74 with a dated document request, and close lower scores unless new evidence changes the inputs. Hard stops override the total: no authorized decision maker, missing required producer authority, or pressure to conceal compensation. Maintain separate health and workers' compensation tracks because the same employer can qualify for one and fail the other. An expiring health renewal may be unsuitable for transition while a documented payroll correction remains actionable. Ask initially for aggregate counts, renewal dates, contract summaries, and redacted worksheets. These establish fit without sending individual claim information through a prospecting platform.

Treat the PBM wedge as a reconciliation problem before treating it as a replacement sale. Normalize National Drug Codes, package units, quantities, dispense dates, retail versus mail channels, and specialty exclusions before comparing claims with CMS NADAC files. NADAC benchmarks pharmacy acquisition costs for covered survey populations; it is neither a universal contract price nor proof of unlawful spread. An illustrative 12,000 eligible fills with a $2 modeled difference creates $24,000 of employer exposure before dispensing fees, rebates, administrative charges, and implementation costs. A $4,000 diagnostic fee is operator revenue if earned; the $24,000 is not. For rebate reconciliation, a verified $100,000 recovery with a permitted 20% collection fee yields $20,000 only under the executed scope and recognition terms. Check licensing and conflicts before offering contingency pricing. Complete a business associate agreement when the service relationship requires one, restrict access by role, encrypt transfers, and define deletion dates. A confidentiality agreement alone does not authorize every disclosure. Use the minimum necessary information where that HIPAA standard applies. If usable records cannot be released, deliver a contract-definition audit using redacted examples and postpone claims repricing. Keep all patient-level information outside outbound CRM notes, demonstration spreadsheets, and email sequences.

Complete the remaining plays with independent evidence paths. TPA service unbundling might support 400 employees at $5 PEPM, or $24,000 annual advisory fees, only when the employer buys genuinely separate work and disclosed compensation avoids hidden overlap. NCCI E-Mod correction starts with the applicable worksheet, payroll periods, loss runs, valuation dates, and carrier reporting history; changes must follow the governing bureau's rules. A modeled $60,000 premium refund and 25% permitted collection split yields $15,000, but no receivable should be assumed from an analyst's estimate. Payroll classification review examines actual duties and state rules rather than searching for the cheapest code. A separate $40,000 collected correction at 20% produces $8,000; exclude amounts already counted in the E-Mod engagement. Partner-led demand comes from payroll firms, benefits counsel, accountants, and licensed brokers with noncompeting specialties. Ten partner conversations yielding three introductions and one paid mandate is a testable planning ratio. Do not pay insurance-related referral compensation before checking the relevant state's licensing and payment restrictions. Where contingency fees, referrals, or delegated administration create unresolved authority issues, use a properly licensed delivery partner or limit the engagement to an authorized fixed-fee analytical scope without negotiating coverage or handling claims.

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks before a mandate becomes delivery work
callout.body: Record the reviewer, evidence, and verification date for each check; an account score never substitutes for these requirements.
items: Verify active Life & Health or Property & Casualty producer authority for the relevant state and activity, plus any applicable TPA or consultant requirements.
Deliver applicable ERISA §408(b)(2)(B) direct and indirect compensation disclosures reasonably before the arrangement, renewal, or extension.

For a coverage transition, compare specific and aggregate attachment points, lasers, exclusions, contract basis, run-out protection, and any RBP balance-bill defense obligations.

sections.heading: 3. Run a measured outreach cadence that sells the smallest useful mandate
paragraphs: Design outbound around one observed event, one bounded hypothesis, and one low-friction request. For a verified acquisition, write: 'Your Item 2.01 filing describes the completed acquisition. If the acquired workforce has separate benefit renewal dates, a contract inventory can identify duplicated administration before renewal. Would a twenty-minute scope call be useful?' Do not claim knowledge of employee health, incumbent misconduct, or undisclosed contract terms. On day zero, send a short business email with the source link; on day two, place a manually dialed business call; on day five, offer a one-page evidence brief; on day nine, make a contextual LinkedIn connection request; on day fourteen, close the sequence with a clear opt-out. A sub-hour EDGAR alert deserves faster initial review, not more aggressive follow-ups. Apply CAN-SPAM identification, accurate headers, a valid postal address, and a functioning opt-out to commercial email. Honor suppression centrally across contractors. Avoid automated texts and prerecorded calls without reviewing the applicable TCPA requirements and state rules. Track reply quality rather than email opens, which are distorted by privacy features and scanners. One useful response is worth more than hundreds of unverified impressions. Keep the cadence at account level so three contacts do not receive simultaneous copies.

Use a cohort funnel to distinguish insufficient demand from poor execution. An illustrative first campaign begins with 300 raw employer records, qualifies 180 against evidence and timing, reaches 150 through valid contact paths, generates 30 positive replies, books 18 discovery calls, secures ten authorized diagnostics, and closes four paid mandates. That means 60% raw-to-qualified, 83.3% qualified-to-reached, 20% reached-to-positive, 60% positive-to-discovery, 55.6% discovery-to-diagnostic, and 40% diagnostic-to-mandate conversion. Overall raw-to-mandate conversion is 1.33%. These are starting hypotheses, not industry benchmarks. If half as many reached accounts respond positively and downstream ratios hold, expect roughly two mandates, subject to small-sample variation. Run weekly cohorts and display counts beside percentages. A signed mandate counts as a win only when scope, price, authority, and payment terms are executed; free calls and broker appointments without billable scope do not count. At $1,800 campaign cash cost and 36 owner hours valued internally at $100, fully loaded acquisition cost is $5,400 divided by four, or $1,350 per mandate. Four $4,000 diagnostics produce $16,000 revenue before delivery costs, not annual recurring revenue. Record both first-cash date and sales-cycle duration, because signed work with delayed collections can exhaust a small operator's working capital.

Support outbound with narrow inbound assets that reveal buying intent without collecting health records. Publish a Form 5500 renewal-date verification worksheet, a PBM rebate-definition checklist, and an E-Mod evidence-request guide. Each should offer a concrete diagnostic deliverable and identify the required source documents. Use a simple website, a scheduling tool, and HubSpot or a controlled spreadsheet for account tracking; no stack purchase compensates for an unclear offer. Host a twenty-minute session with a payroll firm on reconciling job duties to audit records, then invite employers to request a scoped review. Ten attendees requesting three follow-ups and one paid diagnostic provide a measurable local experiment. Keep referral economics separate from education and check state restrictions before sharing insurance-related compensation. Weeks one and two establish licenses, sources, assets, and the first account cohort; weeks three through six test messaging and deliver initial diagnostics; weeks seven through twelve convert evidence into paid mandates; weeks thirteen through twenty repeat only productive channels. The objective is three to ten signed wins within two to five months, with narrower scopes for the first engagements. If delivery capacity is constrained, delay new start dates openly instead of selling a savings implementation the team cannot support.

sections.heading: 4. Resolve objections, protect the mandate, and reconcile retained revenue
paragraphs: Handle incumbent resistance by separating evidence collection from replacement authority. When the employer says the broker already performs this work, ask for the relevant deliverable and compare scope, timing, and compensation without attacking the incumbent. Offer a joint review or withdraw duplicated work. When the objection is disruption, propose a renewal inventory or retrospective reconciliation that leaves coverage unchanged. When the employer demands guaranteed savings, define a paid diagnostic with explicit assumptions and a decision threshold rather than promising a result before seeing contracts. For 'send your best rate,' explain that premiums alone omit attachment points, lasers, exclusions, contract basis, and run-out coverage. Stop-loss pricing can look attractive while transferring materially more risk to the employer. Reference-based pricing requires specific consideration of provider access, balance-bill support, and the contractual defense arrangement; it is not simply a lower reimbursement percentage. If the buyer refuses necessary evidence, narrow the deliverable to what can be supported. Never request a broker-of-record change merely to obtain a conversation. Document the employer's decision criteria before preparing alternatives so the proposal answers a real buying question. A preserved relationship with a useful future renewal date can be worth more than an unsupported immediate sale.

Make the first mandate small enough to deliver well and specific enough to enforce economically. Define the employer entities, covered period, records required, analytical method, exclusions, deliverables, fee basis, termination terms, and correction process. For recovery work, distinguish a modeled error, a carrier-approved adjustment, a posted credit, and cash actually received; define which event earns the fee and how reversals are handled. Do not let the operator receive premiums or claim funds merely because the engagement involves insurance. For covered group health brokerage or consulting arrangements reasonably expecting at least $1,000 in direct or indirect compensation, apply ERISA §408(b)(2)(B) disclosure requirements, including services, applicable fiduciary statements, compensation sources, and payment manner. Deliver the disclosures reasonably before entering, extending, or renewing the arrangement, subject to the statute's specific rules. Verify state requirements independently; an ERISA plan does not erase producer or TPA obligations. A $4,000 diagnostic with $1,200 contractor cost and eight owner hours budgeted at $100 has $2,000 contribution after those delivery inputs, before acquisition and overhead. If the fully loaded acquisition allocation is $1,350, only $650 remains on that initial engagement. Expand recurring work only when the client receives a distinct ongoing service.

Reconcile the acquisition plan to the supplied Formula v2.0 scorecard instead of inflating a small pipeline into an annual result. Conservative revenue of $120,000 less $81,600 total cost produces $38,400 owner net profit at 32%; Base revenue of $535,000 less $294,250 produces $240,750 at 45.0%; Scaled revenue of $950,000 less $399,000 produces $551,000 at 58%. Conservative and Base use one full-time operator plus three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time people plus four contractors. The scorecard's gross-revenue label refers here to retained operator fees and commissions, not underlying employer spending. Apply the ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment to each arrangement; do not mechanically net every subcontractor payment. Where the operator acts as agent and retains 70% of $100,000 fee billings, recognized retained revenue is $70,000, with the other $30,000 excluded from that revenue basis. Do not subtract the $30,000 again as an operating cost. Employer premiums, claim funds, and recovered principal remain outside operator revenue. The startup range is $8,000–$45,000 and monthly operating range is $2,000–$11,000; neither replaces the annual scenarios' all-in costs. Track actual delivery labor, acquisition expense, insurance, systems, and collection delays before increasing outbound volume.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40, Self-Funded Health, PBM & Workers' Comp Arbitrage, holds Rank #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter turns the volume's 11 mapped plays into an evidence-first production line: public-record sourcing, licensed intake, claims normalization, contract verification, fee recognition, and bank reconciliation. Six copy-pasteable engineering modules separate employer money from retained operator fees and serialize every ledger mutation. A worked three-month cohort reaches the $535,000 Base annual revenue run rate without pretending its ramp quarter already earned a steady-state quarter. Formula v2.0 annual owner profits remain $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled. The operating discipline is simple: contract evidence establishes the fee, completed service establishes revenue, and an independent bank statement establishes cash.

sections.heading: 1. Build the intake queue around provable buying triggers
paragraphs: Start with an employer identity, an authorized contact, and a renewal window, not a speculative savings percentage. The public_record_api_intelligence play uses DOL EFAST2 Form 5500 filings, available Schedule A insurance information, and applicable Schedule C service-provider disclosures to identify benefit-plan changes worth investigating. Schedule availability depends on filing rules; an absent schedule does not establish missing compensation or misconduct. Normalize employer EIN, plan number, plan year, filing amendment, and source retrieval date before deduplicating. County dockets can expose an employer restructuring trigger, while state unclaimed-property records can support an expressly authorized recovery inquiry; neither creates a right to claim another party's money. Probate records usually add no value to this employer mandate and stay outside the queue. Across the illustrative cohort, 420 raw records lose 105 duplicates or unsuitable employers, leaving 315 usable targets. At six analyst minutes each, review consumes 31.5 hours; at $60 per hour, the labor allowance is $1,890. Illustrative cached retrieval expense of $0.03 per record adds $12.60. When interfaces fail, switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues rather than bypassing access restrictions.

Treat the volume's 11 mapped plays as eleven operational workstreams here: public-record intelligence, renewal timing, compensation discovery, self-funded feasibility, captive comparison, stop-loss placement, PBM repricing, rebate recovery, payroll classification review, experience-modification correction, and contingent refund collection. This is a coverage checklist, not eleven separate revenue streams. One employer can traverse several workstreams while paying one retained advisory fee. Request a signed engagement, current plan documents, census definitions, carrier authorizations, loss runs, payroll audits, PBM contracts, and a named employer decision-maker. Separate covered employees from covered members because a dependent count error can double a PEPM invoice. Under ERISA section 408(b)(2), including the group-health-plan brokerage and consulting provisions added by CAA 2021, applicable compensation disclosures must identify direct and indirect compensation before the arrangement begins. Florida Statutes section 626.112 illustrates producer licensing requirements; map actual activities and states before solicitation. Use licensed Life and Health and Property and Casualty producers for their respective lines. Pure analysis does not authorize insurance solicitation, and producer status does not automatically authorize TPA functions. Record every limitation in the engagement and route unsupported activities to an appropriately licensed partner under a disclosed agreement.

Assign the founder relationship ownership and final commercial review; use three contractors for actuarial or stop-loss review, PBM analytics, and workers' compensation auditing. Require written scopes, delivery dates, and access boundaries instead of giving every contractor the entire employer dataset. HIPAA business-associate obligations turn on the parties' roles and information handled. Execute applicable agreements under 45 CFR 164.504(e), document permitted uses, and implement minimum-necessary access under 45 CFR 164.514(d). Store clinical files separately from the prospect CRM and fee ledger; those systems need employer identifiers and evidence references, not diagnoses or prescriptions. A tokenized member identifier alone does not establish HIPAA de-identification. The reference intake score gives up to fifty points for covered lives and fifty for a sixty-to-one-hundred-eighty-day renewal window; it prioritizes work rather than estimating savings. An analyst must verify renewal timing against the current contract because Form 5500 filings lag operating reality. Reject prospects without employer authority, required records, or a feasible renewal timetable. Preserve rejection reasons and source hashes so the next campaign does not repeatedly purchase or review the same dead lead.

callout.title: Win the evidence contest before the incumbent controls it
callout.body: Make the employer's source documents and executed contracts the authority for every proposal, invoice, and recovery.
items: Ask for the current stop-loss renewal and expiring contract together; a cheaper quote can hide a new laser, a changed contract basis, or a shortened terminal-liability period.
Reconcile PBM reversals and rebills before comparing ingredient costs; otherwise a single prescription can inflate both the baseline and the advertised recovery.
Order valuation-dated loss runs before challenging an E-Mod; a reserve reduction after the relevant valuation date may affect a later rating period rather than the current one.
Give the employer a compensation inventory early, including override and referral arrangements, so an incumbent cannot turn a late disclosure into a renewal derailment.

sections.heading: 2. Implement an atomic evidence-to-ledger production line
paragraphs: Deploy the six reference modules below into one controlled working directory. Save the SQL cells as schema.sql and reconciliation.sql, and the Python cells as intake.py, workflow.py, settlement.py, and qa.py. Initialize a local SQLite database with both SQL files before accepting work. Use Python 3.9 or later, integer cents, a dedicated operator fee account, and a single authoritative database on local storage; do not place a WAL database on a shared network filesystem. Every writer opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE before reading idempotency or state, so competing workers serialize their check-and-write sequence. Unique request keys prevent repeated commands, natural business keys block duplicate cases, and unique bank references block the same receipt under a different request key. A reused key with changed content raises an error instead of silently accepting altered instructions. The thirty-second lock timeout can reject a busy request; retry the identical durable key after rollback. This removes check-then-insert races within the supported local-database workflow, not every possible infrastructure failure. No module initiates a bank transfer or promises exactly-once behavior from an external payment service. Settlement records only already-observed bank movements.

The verification and escrow state machine is deliberately noncustodial: RECEIVED moves to VERIFIED, then HELD, EARNED, and SETTLED. HELD means the fee entitlement remains on a contractual release checklist; it does not mean this operator holds employer claims money in escrow. Verification requires document references for licensing, disclosures, and source reconciliation. Earning requires completed-service, authorized-fee, and release evidence reviewed by the accountable person. The program checks references and ordering, not the truth of the underlying documents. At EARNED, one balanced posting debits receivables and credits retained operator revenue. At SETTLED, a separately evidenced bank receipt debits cash and credits receivables. Fee candidates and refund estimates never enter revenue merely because intake succeeded. Reject unsupported cases before earning. This compact implementation accepts one exact receipt per earned case and rejects partial payments, overpayments, reversals, mixed remittances, and changed terms. Route those exceptions to a controlled accounting process rather than editing immutable rows. Expand the schema with reviewed allocation and reversing-entry journals before automating those cases. Keep original documents in a permissioned evidence store with checksums; the ledger carries references rather than sensitive source content.

Run intake with a durable request key and a JSON file containing source, external_id, covered_lives, renewal_days, case_id, lane, period, amount_cents, and evidence_ref. The source identity must remain stable across monthly fees; changed source facts require a reviewed revision process rather than a second employer identity. Invoke workflow with database, request key, case identifier, action, and evidence-file arguments. Settlement takes database, request key, and its documented JSON payload; fund and expense use a null case identifier. Apply a restrictive file-access policy because direct database writers could circumvent application transition rules. Keep backups through SQLite's backup API, test restoration, and retain append-only command evidence. The reconciliation view separates contract amounts, earned fees, receipts, and open receivables; summing contracts is not a revenue report. QA checks database integrity, foreign keys, balanced accounts, state consistency, and cash postings against an independently verified statement balance. A matching imported total alone cannot detect a transaction omitted from both imports and postings. Run a separate statement-line completeness review. These reference modules are supplied source, not an executed deployment or a substitute for adversarial concurrency and restore testing in the operator's environment.

BEGIN IMMEDIATE;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS case_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    c.case_id,
    c.lane,
    c.period,
    c.state,
    c.amount_cents AS contracted_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN j.kind = 'earn' THEN j.cents ELSE 0 END
    ), 0) AS earned_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN j.kind = 'receive' THEN j.cents ELSE 0 END
    ), 0) AS received_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE
            WHEN j.kind = 'earn' THEN j.cents
            WHEN j.kind = 'receive' THEN -j.cents
            ELSE 0
        END
    ), 0) AS receivable_cents
FROM cases AS c
LEFT JOIN journal AS j ON j.case_id = c.case_id
GROUP BY c.case_id, c.lane, c.period, c.state, c.amount_cents;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS account_balances AS
SELECT account, SUM(signed_cents) AS debit_balance_cents
FROM (
    SELECT debit AS account, cents AS signed_cents FROM journal
    UNION ALL
    SELECT credit AS account, -cents AS signed_cents FROM journal
)
GROUP BY account;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS cash_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    (
        SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN debit = 'CASH' THEN cents
                WHEN credit = 'CASH' THEN -cents
                ELSE 0
            END
        ), 0)
        FROM journal
    ) AS journal_cash_cents,
    (
        SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
            CASE WHEN direction = 'IN' THEN cents ELSE -cents END
        ), 0)
        FROM bank_transactions
    ) AS imported_bank_cash_cents;

COMMIT;

Inspect case_reconciliation, account_balances, and cash_reconciliation without equating contract pipeline values with earned revenue.
Module six audits a consistent snapshot against independent statement evidence

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
import sys


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise RuntimeError(message)


def audit(db_path, independently_verified_bank_balance_cents):
    connection = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    try:
        connection.execute("BEGIN")
        require(
            connection.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchall() == [("ok",)],
            "SQLite integrity check failed",
        )
        require(
            not connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall(),
            "A foreign-key relationship failed",
        )
        trial = connection.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(debit_balance_cents), 0) FROM account_balances"
        ).fetchone()[0]
        require(trial == 0, "Trial balance does not equal zero")
        bad_cases = connection.execute(
            """
            SELECT case_id FROM case_reconciliation
            WHERE
                (
                    state IN ('RECEIVED', 'VERIFIED', 'HELD', 'REJECTED')
                    AND (earned_cents != 0 OR received_cents != 0)
                )
                OR (
                    state = 'EARNED'
                    AND (
                        earned_cents != contracted_cents
                        OR received_cents != 0
                    )
                )
                OR (
                    state = 'SETTLED'
                    AND (
                        earned_cents != contracted_cents
                        OR received_cents != contracted_cents
                        OR receivable_cents != 0
                    )
                )
            """
        ).fetchall()
        require(not bad_cases, "Case state and posted amounts disagree")
        bad_bank = connection.execute(
            """
            SELECT b.command_key
            FROM bank_transactions AS b
            LEFT JOIN journal AS j ON j.command_key = b.command_key
            WHERE j.entry_id IS NULL
                OR b.cents != j.cents
                OR (b.direction = 'IN' AND j.debit != 'CASH')
                OR (b.direction = 'OUT' AND j.credit != 'CASH')
            UNION ALL
            SELECT j.command_key
            FROM journal AS j
            LEFT JOIN bank_transactions AS b ON b.command_key = j.command_key
            WHERE (j.debit = 'CASH' OR j.credit = 'CASH')
                AND b.command_key IS NULL
            """
        ).fetchall()
        require(not bad_bank, "Bank evidence and cash postings disagree")
        cash, imported = connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM cash_reconciliation"
        ).fetchone()
        require(cash == imported, "Imported cash does not reconcile")
        require(
            cash == independently_verified_bank_balance_cents,
            "Independent statement balance differs from recorded cash",
        )
        connection.commit()
        return {
            "integrity": "passed",
            "trial_balance_cents": trial,
            "reconciled_cash_cents": cash,
        }
    finally:
        if connection.in_transaction:
            connection.rollback()
        connection.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(audit(sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])))

sections.heading: 3. Convert analytical differences into defensible earned fees
paragraphs: For self-funded transitions, build a monthly exposure model from paid and incurred claims, enrollment movements, large claimant detail obtained through authorized channels, and the employer's risk budget. Compare specific and aggregate stop-loss attachment points, aggregate accommodation, contract basis, exclusions, lasers, and terminal liability before comparing premiums. A 12/12 contract and a 12/15 contract do not provide interchangeable payment windows; read the actual policy definitions rather than relying on shorthand. Model an illustrative $250,000 specific attachment separately from a $500,000 claimant laser: the additional $250,000 remains employer exposure for that claimant if the contract so provides. Do not treat that retained risk as operator revenue or available cash. A captive proposal needs the same discipline plus collateral, assessment, exit, and claims-administration terms. Reference-based pricing requires a documented balance-bill defense arrangement and coordinated plan language, not an assumed universal provider acceptance rate. If underwriting deteriorates before binding, reprice, retain the incumbent arrangement, or postpone the transition. The fee ledger should recognize only the operator's completed advisory work and earned placement compensation under the applicable contracts, not projected employer savings.

For PBM work, normalize National Drug Codes, quantities, days supplied, fill dates, pharmacy channels, reversals, and contract definitions before comparing ingredient costs. CMS NADAC provides a useful acquisition-cost benchmark for covered retail observations, but it is not a universal payable price and does not resolve specialty, limited-distribution, dispensing-fee, or rebate economics by itself. An illustrative matched set of 10,000 fills with a $7 ingredient-cost gap creates a $70,000 investigation hypothesis, not an immediately collectible debt. Reconcile exclusions, fees, contract guarantees, rebate timing, and actual payments before alleging an underpayment. A negotiated 20% recovery fee on an accepted $40,000 rebate shortfall produces $8,000 of operator entitlement only when the engagement's earning conditions are satisfied; the employer's remaining $32,000 is not operator revenue. Review gag-clause restrictions under 29 U.S.C. 1185m when contracts impede permitted access to cost or quality information. If claim-level access remains blocked, pursue authorized contractual access and reconcile aggregate remittance evidence; do not fabricate precision from incomplete files. Keep any PBM recovery outside the cohort arithmetic below unless a distinct executed arrangement and receipt support adding that revenue.

For workers' compensation, reconcile audited payroll, classifications, experience periods, claim status, and valuation dates against the governing state's approved rating rules. NCCI methodology is not universal; independent rating bureaus require their own worksheets and dispute routes. A simple diagnostic uses $200,000 of illustrative premium before the experience factor: changing a supported modifier from 1.15 to 1.05 suggests a $20,000 difference before other rating elements. The carrier's corrected calculation, not that shortcut, establishes the actual adjustment. At a 25% contractual split, a collected $20,000 refund produces a $5,000 operator fee and $15,000 of employer benefit. Route the refund directly from carrier to employer wherever the arrangement allows, then invoice the earned fee. Check state producer, administrator, and fee-sharing requirements before signing a contingent arrangement. A class code challenge can also increase premium, so explain the complete corrected result rather than cherry-picking favorable categories. If the carrier disputes the worksheet or a correction window has closed, preserve the evidence, use the applicable review procedure, and leave the contested fee unearned. Separate future premium reductions from retroactive cash refunds throughout the proposal and ledger.

sections.heading: 4. Walk the first ninety operating days into the Base run rate
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk starts after sixty days of relationship development; two Month 1 conversions are previously warmed contacts within that month's source cohort. This respects the volume's two-to-five-month first-deal range instead of promising an immediate cold-start sale. The founder supplies $25,000, spends $5,000 on pre-clock setup, and begins Day 1 with $20,000 of unrestricted operator cash. No owner distributions occur during the walk. Month 1 starts with 120 records, removes thirty, qualifies twelve, signs four employers, and launches two. Month 2 starts with 140 records, removes thirty-five, qualifies fourteen, signs five, and launches four: two carried from Month 1 and two newly signed. Month 3 starts with 160 records, removes forty, qualifies sixteen, signs six, and launches four: three carried from Month 2 and one newly signed. The ending roster therefore contains ten live employers and five signed employers awaiting implementation. Qualified but unsigned opportunities are lost or deferred outside this walk. Use signed effective dates at month start for the modeled full-month PEPM fees; otherwise prorate rather than billing an entire month by assumption.

Each live employer contributes three hundred covered members at a retained $10 PEPM advisory rate. Active counts of two, six, and ten therefore produce $6,000, $18,000, and $30,000 of monthly advisory revenue. Earned retained stop-loss and TPA-related commissions contribute $4,000, $6,000, and $10,000, supported by actual compensation arrangements rather than an assumed percentage of premiums. Collected contingent workers' compensation fees contribute zero, $1,000, and $4,583.33. Those fees correspond to accepted employer refunds of $4,000 and $18,333.32 at a 25% retained split; refund principal never enters operator revenue. The model assumes every month's earned operator fees clear that month, with no opening receivables or unpaid expenses. Actual delayed commissions or refunds must shift cash without accelerating recognition. Month 3 annualizes to $360,000 advisory fees, $120,000 commissions, and $55,000 recovery fees, totaling the canonical $535,000 Base revenue. These are already retained operator amounts. Do not apply another retained-share haircut, and do not gross up employer premiums, claims funds, or refunds into revenue. Document the ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment and contractual earning basis for each arrangement.

Monthly cash operating costs are $11,000, $17,000, and $24,520.83. Each month includes $8,000 of fixed overhead; variable delivery and placement costs are $3,000, $9,000, and $16,520.83. The fixed overhead fits the volume's $2,000-to-$11,000 monthly operating envelope, while total costs explicitly include specialist delivery and other variable expenses. The scorecard does not provide that cost decomposition; this walk states it as a modeling assumption rather than silently equating overhead with total expenses. Monthly operating cash contributions are negative $1,000, positive $8,000, and positive $20,062.50, yielding cumulative operating cash of $27,062.50 and ending bank cash of $47,062.50. The ramp quarter earns $79,583.33, not a steady-state quarter's $133,750. At steady state, annual expenses of $294,250 leave $240,750 owner profit and a 45.0% margin. Allocate the annual rounding pennies explicitly: eight months use $44,583.33 revenue and $24,520.83 costs; four use $44,583.34 and $24,520.84. Both patterns yield $20,062.50 monthly profit. Conservative and Scaled remain $38,400 and $551,000 annual owner profit under their separate canonical staffing and margin assumptions.

sections.heading: 1. Build the public-record spine before buying enrichment
paragraphs: Start with an employer-plan identity spine, not a purchased contact list. Download the Department of Labor Form 5500 datasets, retain each original archive, and key observations by sponsor EIN, plan number, filing year, and amendment status. Preserve sponsor names as reported while keeping a separate normalized matching field. A sponsor can maintain several welfare plans, change administrators, or file an amended return; merging everything under a similar trading name manufactures false renewal opportunities. Schedule A can identify reported insurance contracts and compensation, while Schedule C contains qualifying service-provider reporting where applicable. Neither schedule provides a complete current contract inventory. Filing deadlines, extensions, reporting exemptions, and processing time make these historical discovery records rather than live renewal calendars. Compare two or three filing years, inspect material changes in funding answers and service relationships, and then request the current plan document and renewal schedule from an authorized employer representative. Record the observation date separately from the coverage period. Use SEC submissions for public-company identity corroboration and SAM.gov for relevant contractor entities, but never infer that a corporate subsidiary shares its parent's benefit arrangements. A clean identity crosswalk prevents expensive repricing work on the wrong population.

Organize the eleven mapped plays as explicit work queues: Form 5500 renewal targeting; broker compensation reconstruction; self-funded transition screening; captive participation screening; stop-loss attachment and laser review; run-out exposure reconstruction; NADAC-based PBM repricing; rebate recovery reconciliation; reference-based pricing defense review; Workers' Comp classification and E-Mod correction; and saas_technographic_churn_pixel_scraping. These work-queue labels describe this chapter's operating decomposition rather than additional supplied play identifiers. Every queue needs an entry document, a calculation, an authorized reviewer, and an exit artifact. For example, renewal targeting starts with a filing observation, calculates days until a verified policy anniversary, and exits with a dated meeting brief. Compensation reconstruction starts with engagement letters and carrier statements, separates direct employer fees from indirect remuneration, and exits with an ERISA section 408(b)(2) disclosure package where the health-plan brokerage or consulting provisions apply. Captive screening requires participation terms and collateral requirements, not just an attractive quote. Reference-based pricing review requires actual provider-dispute and defense terms, not a generic savings percentage. Give each queue a reason to stop: unavailable authority, unmatched policy, incomplete claim period, or unresolved allocation. Such stops preserve analyst capacity for evidence that can support a transaction.

Use the first nine directory entries as a low-cost discovery and reference layer. CMS NADAC provides acquisition-cost benchmarks, not a complete measure of an employer's contractual drug cost. Preserve effective dates, units, package identifiers, and the original extract before joining it to an authorized pharmacy claim. RxNav and the FDA NDC Directory help resolve identifiers, but neither substitutes for the PBM's paid-claim ledger or establishes therapeutic equivalence. NPPES identifies providers; an NPI does not establish network participation, credentialing status, or payment entitlement. Transparency in Coverage files can support selected negotiated-rate comparisons, yet their size, reporting relationships, and plan-specific applicability make broad downloads wasteful. Fetch a relevant index first, isolate the required payer and service family, and cap storage before expanding. A five-gigabyte partition downloaded twice consumes ten gigabytes of transfer without adding evidence; content hashes and conditional requests avoid that duplication. Treat every published cadence as the publisher's intended schedule, with observed release timestamps controlling analysis. Public availability also does not imply permission to redistribute every assembled product. Store source terms alongside each connector, and send stale or incomplete observations into a document-request queue rather than silently substituting a more convenient benchmark.
