sections.heading: 2. Buy restricted evidence selectively and treat technographics as weak signals
paragraphs: The second nine directory entries handle restricted rating evidence, producer verification, and enrichment. NCCI and WCIRB materials are not open employer-loss databases: access depends on the product, jurisdiction, subscriber agreement, and permitted relationship to the insured. Obtain employer authority and request the applicable issued worksheet before building any E-Mod correction model. Separate classification questions from experience-rating questions because payroll allocation, loss valuation, ownership changes, and state rules affect different calculations. Use state insurance-department records as the primary check for producer license status and authorized lines; NIPR reports can consolidate permitted information but do not replace state-specific analysis. Record both the producer and business-entity requirements applicable to the engagement. A Life and Health license does not authorize Property and Casualty placement, and an advisory label does not resolve whether TPA licensing applies to actual activities. Keep license verification outside the prospect scoring model: it determines whether the proposed service can be performed, not whether the account looks attractive. Where access is unavailable, request the employer's existing worksheet, policy declarations, payroll audit, and loss runs through the current authorized channel. Never purchase another party's portal credentials or route restricted records through a general-purpose enrichment vendor.

Implement saas_technographic_churn_pixel_scraping as TRACK_1 commercial-domain observation, not employee tracking. For each approved target, inspect public homepage script hosts and permitted DNS TXT/CNAME records weekly for Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Segment, and NetSuite indicators. Store the observation timestamp, response hash, matching rule version, and previous state. Weekly polling cannot establish the exact installation or removal day: it yields an interval between the last confirmed old state and first confirmed new state. Record an exact event date only when a reliable dated source supports it. A historical first-seen event can generate a Month 10–11 hypothesis, never a verified software or benefits renewal. With 200 domains, three requests per domain, and 52 weekly runs, the planned workload is 31,200 requests annually before retries; per-host pacing matters more than aggregate speed. If twenty monthly changes produce six corroborated migrations, a thirty-minute review of each corroborated event consumes three analyst hours. Those figures describe screening workload, not promised conversion. Marketing agencies, tag managers, cached pages, and domain redirects all create false events. Suppress a lead until a second observation or employer confirmation distinguishes migration from routine website maintenance.

Build the enrichment waterfall from cheapest and least intrusive evidence upward. First resolve the legal entity from filings; then inspect its public website and DNS; next use a licensed historical-DNS or technographic service only for unresolved accounts; finally write qualified employer-level facts into the desk's authorized CRM. SecurityTrails and BuiltWith can corroborate historical observations, but their coverage and collection dates differ, so agreement between vendors is not proof of an independent underlying event. The required fallback combines passive DNS TXT/CNAME observations with dated job-posting mentions and then seeks direct confirmation before routing a claimed vendor switch. Job descriptions can remain online after a migration, so preserve publication and retrieval dates separately. HubSpot company records should contain evidence links, source age, and outreach rationale, not member claims or prescription histories. Use narrowly scoped private-app tokens or OAuth grants for the operator's own account, and rotate access when contractors leave. A hypothetical $150 monthly enrichment subscription spread across thirty reviewed accounts costs $5 per reviewed account before labor; attribute that expense within the scenario's operating-cost envelope rather than inventing incremental profit. When paid evidence adds no corroboration, cancel the connector and retain the public-record workflow.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile diagnostic tools to claims, rating documents, and retained revenue
paragraphs: A useful PBM diagnostic separates paid ingredient cost, dispensing fees, administrative charges, member cost sharing, rebates, and other contractual remuneration. Obtain an employer-authorized, appropriately protected claim extract and a data dictionary before calculating anything. Match reversals and resubmissions, preserve service dates, and normalize quantities only with a documented conversion. For an illustrative fill of thirty units, a $2.10 NADAC benchmark produces $63 of benchmark ingredient cost; a comparable $78 ingredient charge leaves a $15 diagnostic difference before dispensing fees, administrative charges, and rebate treatment. One thousand comparable fills would produce $15,000 of benchmark difference, not established recoverable savings and not desk revenue. Actual recovery requires contractual entitlement, suitable comparability, and a settled employer credit. Rebate analysis must match covered drug periods, eligible utilization, guarantee definitions, exclusions, and reconciliation dates. If an employer receives $40,000 and the desk's enforceable retained split is 20%, the associated fee basis is $8,000 when recognition conditions are met; the remaining $32,000 never becomes operator revenue. Where specialty products lack suitable benchmarks, segregate them and request contract-specific evidence. Do not extrapolate the clean generic sample across excluded specialty utilization merely to enlarge the proposal.

Workers' Comp diagnostics need an equally disciplined distinction between an indicative model and an issued correction. With $1,000,000 of payroll and a hypothetical manual rate of $4 per $100, the manual premium component is $40,000. Multiplying that component by 1.20 rather than 1.10 changes it by $4,000 before schedule factors, credits, assessments, minimums, and other policy adjustments. This sensitivity calculation does not establish the actual corrected premium or prove that the experience modifier should change. Reproduce the applicable bureau rules, valuation dates, split points, payroll classifications, and loss treatment using authorized records; then submit documented discrepancies through the proper carrier or bureau process. Stop-loss analysis needs a separate worksheet containing specific and aggregate attachment points, named lasers, contract basis, aggregating deductibles, and run-in or run-out treatment. A $250,000 specific attachment with a $500,000 claimant laser leaves an additional $250,000 of claimant-specific exposure under otherwise comparable terms; model that exposure rather than counting premium reduction alone. If claim detail or policy wording remains incomplete, obtain a binding clarification or compare documented alternatives. Captive collateral and reference-based pricing defense obligations belong in the employer risk model, never in the desk's sales-revenue column.

Keep the scorecard ledger separate from all employer savings and insurance flows. Formula v2.0 defines Conservative revenue of $120,000 at 32%, producing $38,400 owner profit and $81,600 costs; Base revenue of $535,000 at 45.0%, producing $240,750 profit and $294,250 costs; and Scaled revenue of $950,000 at 58%, producing $551,000 profit and $399,000 costs. Teams remain 1 FT plus 3 C in Conservative and Base, and 2 FT plus 4 C in Scaled. Although the scorecard calls the topline gross revenue, its stated basis is already net retained operator fees, commissions, and refund splits. Do not apply an invented retained-share discount a second time. An illustrative Base composition is 2,500 covered employees times $10 retained PEPM times twelve months, or $300,000, plus $175,000 retained stop-loss/TPA commissions and $60,000 collected refund splits. The last component could represent a 25% retained share of $240,000 settled employer refunds. These components total exactly $535,000 and are a reconciliation example, not extra revenue assumptions. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent presentation to the actual arrangements and evaluate variable consideration and performance obligations. Cash collection, signed engagement, and revenue recognition are distinct ledger events.

sections.heading: 4. Operate a reproducible pipeline with bounded access and evidence-backed handoffs
paragraphs: Use a three-zone pipeline: immutable source objects, normalized working records, and approved employer-level outputs. A small desk can implement control tables with SQLite, transformations with Python's csv, decimal, datetime, hashlib, and json modules, and scheduled execution through its existing job runner. These choices avoid unnecessary subscription sprawl, but the standard library alone does not provide encrypted databases or managed secrets. Place files on appropriately encrypted storage, keep tokens in an approved credential service, and apply account-level access controls. Every ingestion manifest should contain source URL or delivery channel, retrieval time, effective period, content hash, authorization reference, schema version, row count, and control totals. Use Decimal for money and explicit currency fields; binary floating-point arithmetic can create avoidable penny mismatches across large claim files. Record rejected rows with a specific reason and reconcile accepted plus rejected counts to the source. Idempotent loading should recognize an identical object and skip duplication while preserving a new amendment as a separate version. Separate network failures from legitimate empty datasets. An empty response after a timeout is not evidence that a broker relationship disappeared or a claim population fell to zero.

Build protections around the actual data role. Public plan filings belong in the discovery zone; member-level claim records belong in a restricted analytical workspace with access limited to the engagement team. Determine whether the desk acts as a business associate and execute required arrangements under 45 CFR 164.502(e) and 164.504(e) before receiving protected health information in that role. Apply minimum-necessary requirements where applicable under 45 CFR 164.502(b), and implement access, audit, integrity, and transmission safeguards under 45 CFR 164.312. Hashing member identifiers alone does not establish HIPAA de-identification; use a supported method under 45 CFR 164.514 when that outcome is required. Keep claims out of CRM notes, ordinary email attachments, public issue trackers, and commercial technographic APIs. Give contractors engagement-specific access and remove it at assignment end. Establish retention periods from contractual duties, applicable rules, and litigation holds, then verify deletion across working copies and backups according to the approved schedule. For an outbound report, inspect the actual recipient list and deliver through the agreed secure channel. Employer-level aggregate findings still require review for small-cell disclosure and contractual restrictions; aggregation is a technique, not an automatic permission to publish.

Run the desk on an exception dashboard rather than a pile of connector success messages. Track source age, unmatched employer identities, missing authorization references, claim-total differences, unresolved product conversions, stale license checks, and proposals lacking a current renewal document. Give every exception an owner and an explicit next action. Test connectors with saved, authorized fixtures so a vendor outage cannot silently change the analytical result. A schema change that renames a paid-amount column must stop the affected calculation, while an optional website-description change should not halt unrelated work. Use bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter, honor Retry-After where provided, and stop after the connector's configured retry budget. Review a small sample of accepted records as well as rejected records; perfectly reconciled totals can still hide a wrong join. At weekly handoff, the analyst supplies the evidence manifest, calculation version, open assumptions, and exact client question. The licensed producer confirms service scope and commercial disclosures before recommendations leave the desk. Measure useful throughput as verified employer briefs and resolved discrepancies per analyst hour, not harvested rows. This discipline supports the scorecard's small teams without pretending automation eliminates underwriting uncertainty, carrier judgment, or client-specific professional review.

chapters.question_prompt: Which federal/state statutes, licensing boundaries, contract clauses, and compliant outreach scripts govern self-funded health, pbm & workers' comp arbitrage?
chapters.title: Contracts, Statutory Guardrails, Licensing & Outreach Scripts
chapters.subtitle: ERISA Compensation Disclosures, State Producer and TPA Boundaries, Stop-Loss Run-Out, PBM Audit Rights, and Permissioned Employer Outreach
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40, Self-Funded Health, PBM & Workers' Comp Arbitrage, ranks #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 11 mapped plays depend on enforceable fee rights, correctly licensed activities, usable claims evidence, and disciplined employer outreach. This chapter connects ERISA §408(b)(2), CAA 2021 disclosures, state producer and TPA rules, HIPAA, stop-loss wording, PBM audit access, and workers' compensation refund authority to executable contracts and scripts. Canonical annual owner profits are $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled. Those profits arise from retained advisory fees, commissions, and earned refund splits, never employer claim funds or premiums. Use the matrices to assign responsible parties, preserve recovery evidence, and stop work when a license, authorization, or contract right is missing.

sections.heading: 1. Assign each service to its federal authority and state license boundary
paragraphs: Start with the employer, plan type, employee locations, and the actual service being sold, not the label benefits consultant. ERISA §408(b)(2)(B), codified at 29 U.S.C. §1108(b)(2)(B), requires covered group health brokerage and consulting providers expecting at least $1,000 in direct or indirect compensation to disclose specified services, compensation, and relationships to the responsible plan fiduciary. Deliver the disclosure reasonably before the contract, extension, or renewal; identify PEPM charges, carrier commissions, overrides, referral payments, and contingent compensation with their payers and calculation methods. A broker-of-record letter is neither that disclosure nor a services agreement. Record the statutory deadlines for changes and corrections rather than assuming annual delivery is sufficient. ERISA §404 requires fiduciaries to evaluate prudence and loyalty; a contract cannot erase fiduciary status created by discretionary functions. Distinguish the employer's business decision to change benefits from fiduciary administration of the adopted plan. Governmental and qualifying church plans are generally outside ERISA Title I, so route those prospects through their applicable public-sector or other governing framework. One $2,000 monthly engagement already exceeds the disclosure threshold; dividing its invoices among affiliates does not justify omitting indirect compensation.

Hold active resident and necessary nonresident Life and Health and Property and Casualty producer licenses for the work performed; confirm each state's exact line names, business-entity requirements, designated responsible producer, and carrier appointments. California Insurance Code §§1621 and 1626 distinguish relevant producer capacities, while New York Insurance Law §2102 prohibits unlicensed insurance producer activity. Texas Insurance Code Chapter 4151 separately governs administrators, subject to its definitions and exemptions. Collecting premium, administering benefits, adjudicating claims, or representing an insured in a coverage settlement can cross additional TPA or adjuster boundaries. A payroll classification review does not automatically authorize negotiating an insurance claim. Stop-loss is insurance even when the employer health plan is self-funded; verify the state's applicable producer authority and stop-loss restrictions before quoting. ERISA preemption is not a universal exemption for insurers, MEWAs, or every PBM practice. NCCI rules also cannot be copied unchanged into California's WCIRB system, independent rating bureau states, or monopolistic state-fund arrangements. For a three-state employer, maintain three completed authority records before solicitation requires those permissions. If a state requires authority the firm lacks, engage a properly licensed specialist under a permitted compensation arrangement or exclude that activity expressly from scope.

Treat claims access as a separate workstream from prospecting. A public Form 5500 does not authorize receipt of identifiable medical or pharmacy claims. Determine whether the advisory firm is a business associate, execute the required business associate agreement, and apply 45 CFR §§164.502(e), 164.504(e), and 164.514(d) to permitted uses and minimum necessary access where applicable. Plan-sponsor access also requires attention to §164.504(f), including plan documents and separation from employment functions. Begin feasibility work with enrollment totals and appropriately de-identified summaries; removing names alone does not establish HIPAA de-identification. For workers' compensation, §164.512(l) permits specified disclosures authorized by applicable law, not unrestricted reuse for benefits sales. CAA gag-clause restrictions under 29 U.S.C. §1185m support specified price and quality information access, but do not override privacy safeguards. Request field definitions, permitted recipient terms, and a secure transfer path before requesting records. Use role-based SharePoint access or an appropriately configured secure portal with suitable contractual coverage, not ordinary outreach inboxes. At 800 covered employees, an 800-row eligibility file may answer a pricing question that would otherwise expose 80,000 claim lines. Escalate missing authorization to the plan administrator and pause identifiable data transfer until the necessary permissions are documented.

sections.heading: 2. Write contracts around fee evidence, coverage continuity, and usable data
paragraphs: Make the master services agreement describe deliverables, exclusions, named decision-makers, and evidence required for acceptance. A benefits advisory schedule can say, 'Monthly advisory fees equal eligible enrolled employees multiplied by the stated PEPM rate; the parties reconcile additions and terminations against the administrator's agreed enrollment report.' Specify whether covered lives, employees, or contracts are counted. For refunds, use, 'The recovery fee becomes payable only after the employer receives an attributable cash refund or an agreed usable premium credit, supported by the carrier's written adjustment.' Exclude projected savings, duplicate recoveries, unrelated audit credits, and carrier reversals. On a $120,000 collected recovery with a 25% fee, the operator earns $30,000; the other $90,000 remains employer value. A documented dispute over $20,000 should not silently produce a fee on the original estimate. Define whether the undisputed portion can be invoiced and how later reversals are refunded. Use narrowly defined anti-circumvention language covering identified introductions or documented findings for a reasonable period, not perpetual ownership of the employer relationship. State that producer compensation follows applicable licensing and commission-sharing rules. If the employer rejects contingency terms, offer a fixed-scope audit with an agreed price and no implied authority to bind coverage.

Attach a stop-loss comparison that shows specific and aggregate attachment points, eligible expense definitions, policy basis, reimbursement timing, disclosure obligations, and run-in or run-out treatment. A 12/12 policy and a 12/15 policy can produce different recoveries for the same service date because payment timing matters; confirm the carrier's definitions rather than relying on shorthand. With a $100,000 specific attachment and $180,000 of otherwise eligible paid claims for one person, the preliminary specific excess is $80,000. A $250,000 laser for that person can reduce that reimbursement to zero. Aggregate protection is calculated under its own terms and cannot be assumed to fill the difference. Require written laser information, terminal liability options, incurred-but-unpaid claim estimates, and transition responsibilities before an employer changes administrators or funding arrangements. Separate any advance-funding accommodation from the carrier's ultimate reimbursement obligation. For reference-based pricing, specify the pricing methodology, provider negotiation process, member communications, balance-bill defense provider, exclusions, and funding of settlements. The No Surprises Act, including 42 U.S.C. §300gg-111, protects specified situations rather than every out-of-network encounter. If defense or transition coverage is unresolved, compare a conventional network alternative and postpone the proposed transition instead of presenting an incomplete savings estimate.

Give the PBM schedule operational definitions for rebates, administrative fees, price concessions, spread, affiliated pharmacy payments, specialty classifications, and settlement timing. State which amounts pass through, what evidence supports reconciliation, and whether audit rights survive termination. NADAC is a useful acquisition-cost benchmark, not a complete employer net-cost measure; add dispensing fees, guarantees, exclusions, rebates, and claims eligibility before comparing alternatives. Require an accessible export specification rather than accepting a dashboard as the sole record. The employer or plan retains its contractual rights in supplied records; the operator retains pre-existing analytical code, subject to confidentiality and tightly bounded data-use permissions. Ownership language does not create a right to sell health information. Negotiate a liability cap proportionate to fees, insurance, and risk, with separately negotiated treatment of confidentiality breaches, fraud, and other excluded liabilities. Do not assume a cap can excuse ERISA fiduciary responsibility; 29 U.S.C. §1110 restricts exculpatory provisions. Specify notice, cure, mediation or litigation venue, collection of undisputed fees, and emergency remedies for data misuse. Require transition exports, retention periods, subcontractor controls, and incident reporting on termination. If a vendor refuses claim-level verification, price the engagement as a limited review and exclude unverifiable recovery promises from compensation calculations.

callout.title: Contract details experienced benefits operators settle before renewal
callout.body: The highest-value negotiation often removes an ambiguous denominator, inaccessible record, or uninsured transition exposure.
items: Attach a sample PEPM invoice with employee-count rules; test one midmonth hire, one termination, and one retroactive eligibility correction.
Build a claim-date and payment-date transition grid before comparing stop-loss prices; price run-out responsibility separately from quoted premium.
Request a small, authorized PBM export sample before signing so NDC identifiers, reversals, rebates, and paid-date fields can actually be reconciled.
Obtain the carrier's written correction and credit allocation before invoicing an E-Mod recovery; a revised worksheet alone does not establish collected employer value.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile eleven operating plays without inflating recognized revenue
paragraphs: Implement the volume's 11 mapped plays through a working register covering renewal targeting, PEPM advisory, self-funded transition analysis, captive evaluation, stop-loss placement, TPA selection, PBM repricing, rebate reconciliation, payroll classification review, E-Mod recovery, and outbound infrastructure. These are operating workstreams, not assertions that every activity has the same licensing treatment. Form 5500 Schedules A and C can expose useful insurance and service-provider information where filed, but exemptions, reporting lags, and plan changes make them leads rather than current authority to quote. Confirm renewal dates directly. For illustrative unit economics, 500 employees at $8 PEPM generate $48,000 annually before any separately disclosed commissions; four equivalent accounts generate $192,000. A captive assessment must include collateral, assessments, exit restrictions, and governing documents, not just a premium comparison. TPA selection needs claims-service standards and export rights, while stop-loss placement needs the coverage comparison already described. PBM repricing and rebate recovery should have separate baselines so the same dollar is not counted twice. Payroll classification and experience-modification corrections require distinct documentary trails. Assign a named owner, permitted activity, compensation basis, and fallback to every workstream. The fallback for incomplete evidence is a bounded diagnostic, never a fabricated recovery estimate.

The mandatory play multi_inbox_free_workspace_outbound_clusters describes 300 or more subsidized mailboxes sending 15–25 plain-text messages daily across secondary domains. Its arithmetic needs qualification: 300 inboxes multiplied by 25 messages and 20 sending days equals 150,000 attempted monthly messages; at 15 messages the same estate produces 90,000. Neither figure establishes acceptance, primary-inbox placement, qualified meetings, or revenue. Avoiding $6–$12 retail seat pricing suggests $1,800–$3,600 monthly gross seat-cost savings before domains, administration, relay charges, and security overhead. Microsoft 365 developer or partner benefits must expressly permit the proposed commercial use; sandbox access is not production entitlement. Cloudflare Email Routing forwards incoming mail and is not an outbound SMTP service. Use approved production accounts and a relay that permits the actual traffic. A maximum of two or three domains per tenant can be an administrative limit, but is not permission to fragment identities or evade provider restrictions. Remove open and click tracking, authenticate sender domains, and honor suppression across all accounts. Catch-all SMTP checks cannot verify every recipient and can encounter provider restrictions. Do not swap domains to bypass complaints or blocks; the fallback is to pause, investigate, reduce volume, and resume only through authorized infrastructure.

Keep the canonical Formula v2.0 cases separate from illustrative sales combinations. Conservative recognized operator revenue is $120,000 with $81,600 of scenario costs, leaving $38,400 at 32% margin and a team of 1 FT plus 3 C. Base revenue is $535,000 with $294,250 of costs, leaving $240,750 at 45.0% with the same staffing. Scaled revenue is $950,000 with $399,000 of costs, leaving $551,000 at 58% with 2 FT plus 4 C. Although the source labels these amounts gross revenue, their defined basis is retained operator fees, commissions, and earned recovery splits, excluding employer claim funds and insurance premiums. Do not subtract a retained share twice. For a billing pool of $100,000 where the operator is an agent entitled to 30%, recognized revenue is $30,000 under the applicable principal-agent analysis, not $100,000; determine that status from contractual control rather than cash routing alone. Match contingent revenue to the earned right and applicable variable-consideration constraint, while separately forecasting cash collections. The $2,000–$11,000 monthly operating range is not a substitute for each scenario's complete annual cost base. Budget startup capital of $8,000–$45,000 and a 2–5 month first-deal interval without treating unsigned pipeline or client reserves as available operating cash.

sections.heading: 4. Use exact outreach scripts, qualify authority, and preserve the audit trail
paragraphs: Use an identifiable commercial email with accurate routing information and a truthful subject, then satisfy 15 U.S.C. §7704 requirements for advertising identification where required, a valid physical postal address, and a functioning opt-out. Populate the actual sender identity, employer, observed filing year, and address before sending; never invent those facts to complete a template. The following body is ready to use once the signature supplies those verified particulars: 'This is a commercial introduction about employer benefits advisory services. We review self-funded plan costs, PBM contract economics, and workers' compensation rating records. A public filing can help us identify a potential renewal conversation, but it does not establish your current funding arrangement or savings opportunity. Would a twenty-minute discussion with the person responsible for benefits purchasing be useful? We do not need employee medical information for that discussion. Reply stop to end our commercial outreach.' Honor opt-outs within ten business days and propagate suppression across every sender and vendor; retain the minimum suppression record needed to avoid recontact. Do not make suppression conditional on a fee or additional personal information. Public contact information and successful mailbox validation do not themselves establish permission or override service-provider restrictions.

For a manually dialed business discovery call, first check applicable federal and state calling restrictions, internal suppression, number type, and any recording requirements. Do not treat B2B labeling as a blanket exemption for automated calls, prerecorded voices, texts, or state rules. Use this opening: 'I am calling about your employer benefits purchasing process. Is this a suitable time for two questions, or should I end the call?' If invited, continue: 'Who controls the benefits services agreement, and when does the next renewal decision occur? Is the medical plan insured or self-funded? Which states have employees, and which administrator and PBM currently serve the plan? Please do not share diagnoses, names of high-cost claimants, or employee identifiers.' Then qualify the workers' compensation work: 'Which carrier and rating bureau issued the policy and experience worksheet? Has the carrier already adjusted the payroll audit or returned any premium for the periods you want reviewed?' Close with: 'The next step is an authorized document checklist and a written scope, not a carrier change. Our compensation sources will be disclosed before engagement.' If the recipient declines, record the preference immediately and end the sales discussion rather than moving the same person into another inbox sequence.

When the employer asks for pricing, say: 'Our proposal will separate monthly advisory fees, insurance commissions, and any recovery fee. Employer premiums and claim reserves are not our revenue. A contingency fee applies only to the recovery defined in the agreement, with an adjustment process for reversals. We will show the calculation before you sign.' When an incumbent requests patient files during the introduction, respond: 'We are not transferring identifiable claims through this email thread. The plan administrator must establish the authorized purpose, recipient, and secure delivery process first.' Preserve these exchanges alongside the proposal, compensation disclosure, signed scope, license checks, and delivery receipts. A practical sequence is public-source qualification, permissioned discovery, authorized limited review, and contracted execution; each stage has its own evidence requirements. For a 40-account pilot, track delivered messages, positive replies, qualified meetings, signed engagements, and collected fees separately. Four meetings do not equal four clients, and a signed contingency contract does not equal earned revenue. Review complaints, bounces, opt-outs, and licensing exceptions weekly. If any outsourced sender cannot demonstrate shared suppression and truthful identity, stop that vendor's campaign while preserving the records needed to investigate and prevent repeat contact.

sections.heading: 1. Build a Renewal Radar That Produces Evidence, Not Prospect Fiction
paragraphs: Start with a tenant-separated evidence ledger, not a conversational agent allowed to browse every employer document. The first three mapped plays are Schedule A/C renewal radar, sponsor entity resolution, and renewal readiness scoring. Download Department of Labor Form 5500 public datasets through documented distribution endpoints; use Python urllib.request, csv, zipfile, hashlib, and sqlite3 to preserve source checksums, filing years, amendments, and extraction versions. Index sponsors by EIN plus plan number, then distinguish legal entities from trade names before joining CRM records. Schedule A can reveal insurance contracts and reported commissions; Schedule C can identify reportable service-provider compensation subject to its reporting rules. Neither schedule is a complete current broker ledger, and self-funded arrangements do not uniformly produce a useful Schedule A insurance record. A plan year-end is a targeting clue, not proof of the renewal date. Store inferred dates separately from employer-confirmed dates. For an illustrative batch of 200 filings, suppose 160 pass parsing, 120 resolve to distinct sponsors, and 30 match the agency's geography and employee band. Those 30 are research candidates, not qualified opportunities. Route ambiguous EIN matches, amended returns, and conflicting provider names to a contractor before any outreach references them.

Make every ingestion event reproducible. A webhook receiver validates an HMAC signature against the raw request body with hmac.compare_digest, rejects stale timestamps, and records a tenant-scoped event identifier before acknowledging receipt. Place accepted jobs in a durable queue; a small deployment can use SQLite transactions with a single dispatcher, moving to a managed queue when concurrency exceeds that design. Keep source documents immutable and write derived records under separate versioned keys. A structured extraction request asks the language model for field values, page references, and quoted supporting text, never permission to contact a prospect or alter a policy. Treat retrieved documents as evidence rather than instructions. Python validates dates, currency units, and required fields after the model responds. A model-generated confidence score cannot establish correctness; compare a labeled sample against human extraction and measure field-level accuracy. For example, 198 correct renewal-date classifications in 200 reviewed records yields 99% sample accuracy, while the two errors still require investigation. Retry transient service failures with capped exponential backoff and jitter. After three unsuccessful attempts, park the job with its source reference and owner. Do not silently manufacture a date to keep the funnel moving. An unavailable model should leave deterministic parsing and manual review operational.

Assign responsibility before increasing throughput. In the 1 FT + 3 C configuration, the full-time principal owns licensed recommendations and commercial relationships; contractors cover benefits and PBM analysis, workers' compensation auditing, and automation plus research operations. These are work allocations, not a claim that every contractor needs equal hours or identical credentials. Verify applicable Life & Health, Property & Casualty, agency, appointment, and TPA requirements against the actual activities and jurisdictions. Keep employer prospect data outside the protected claims workspace. Where the operator is a business associate, execute the required agreement and apply HIPAA access, disclosure, and security requirements before handling protected health information. Public filing availability does not authorize access to employee claims. Use role-based access, tenant-specific exports, encrypted storage, and an approved retention schedule. Renewal scoring should favor confirmed decision timing, accessible plan documents, employer size fit, and an identifiable decision-maker, rather than diagnoses or individual claimant characteristics. A 40-point readiness score might allocate ten points to each of those four dimensions, with a documented rule for every awarded point. Publish the evidence links beside the score. When the employer corrects a filing-derived assumption, preserve the correction history and replace the active value instead of overwriting the original source. That provenance prevents stale automation from repeatedly reopening settled questions.

sections.heading: 2. Automate PBM and E-Mod Arithmetic While Reserving Judgment for Specialists
paragraphs: The next four mapped plays are the NADAC comparator, rebate reconciliation, E-Mod replay, and payroll-code audit. Build the PBM pipeline around an authorized claim extract, current contract, eligibility periods, formulary terms, and rebate settlement statements. Normalize NDC identifiers only with a documented conversion rule; retain the original identifier because package and product confusion can destroy unit math. Match CMS NADAC observations to the dispensing date and compatible units, recording publication date and effective date separately. NADAC measures surveyed retail community pharmacy acquisition costs; it does not automatically establish the contracted price for every specialty, mail, or excluded product. Suppose 100 eligible fills contain 30 tablets each, the matched benchmark is $0.12 per tablet, the illustrative dispensing allowance is $1.50, and employer-paid cost after member cost-sharing adjustments is $9.00 per fill. The comparator is $5.10 per fill and the observed difference is $390 across the cohort. Call that a benchmark difference, not recoverable spread or promised savings. A specialist must reconcile taxes, fees, channel, reversals, member liability, and contractual definitions before presenting an actionable finding. Unmatched products stay outside the calculated cohort and appear in a coverage report, so a small clean subset cannot masquerade as a whole-book conclusion.

Rebate reconciliation requires a separate settlement model because a low ingredient price and a high rebate can describe different economic arrangements. Parse the contract's eligible claims, exclusions, minimum guarantees, allocation periods, administrative deductions, and payment deadlines into a reviewed rule sheet. For an illustrative quarter, 1,000 eligible claims at an $18 contractual minimum produce an $18,000 minimum settlement before contract-specific adjustments. If $14,000 has been credited and no adjustment applies, the $4,000 difference is a reconciliation item requiring evidence, not immediately recognized agency revenue. The employer's recovered amount and the operator's earned fee occupy different ledger accounts. Under a hypothetical 20% earned recovery split, a collected $4,000 recovery produces $800 of operator fee revenue, subject to the actual agreement and recognition conditions. Never add the $4,000 employer recovery to the $800 fee. Use Decimal for money, explicit rounding rules, and tests for reversed claims and duplicated settlement files. Models can classify clauses and draft discrepancy letters, but a benefits specialist verifies every contract citation and the licensed principal releases the communication. If eligible-claim counts disagree, suspend the dollar demand and send a narrow request for the missing settlement detail. Preserve the original calculation so later evidence changes the estimate transparently rather than rewriting the audit trail.

For workers' compensation, obtain the employer-authorized rating worksheet, policy documents, loss runs, payroll detail, and applicable NCCI or independent-bureau rules. E-Mod replay means reproducing the bureau's calculation using the correct state, experience period, expected-loss rates, split points, credibility components, and rule effective dates. It does not mean subtracting an inconvenient claim from total losses. Licensed access terms govern proprietary manuals and data; automation must use permitted exports rather than circumventing access controls. The payroll-code audit separately compares payroll records, actual duties, classification rules, officer treatment, and permitted payroll divisions. Consider a simplified premium component with $1,000,000 payroll, a $2.00 rate per $100 payroll, and a 1.20 modifier. That component is $24,000; substituting a verified 1.10 modifier yields $22,000, a $2,000 difference before other policy charges and adjustments. At a hypothetical 25% earned refund split, a collected $2,000 refund generates $500 operator revenue. Label this as illustrative component arithmetic, not a complete premium quotation. A workers' compensation specialist checks state-specific correction procedures and deadlines before submission. If the replay cannot match the issued worksheet, freeze the correction package and reconcile inputs with the carrier or bureau. Never reclassify hazardous duties solely because a cheaper code improves the displayed result.

sections.heading: 3. Measure Automation by Completed Work and Reconcile Every Dollar
paragraphs: The eighth mapped play, exception routing, converts the three analysis pipelines into a controlled service operation. Establish a fixed taxonomy of repetitive tasks before claiming 70% automation. In an illustrative week containing 100 comparable task instances, let 30 concern research, 20 qualification, 35 fulfillment preparation, and 15 distribution administration. If 25, 16, 26, and seven respectively finish without manual rework, the automation rate is 74%. Count an instance once; a failed extraction retried four times is not four successes. Record human review minutes separately, including final reviews of automatically prepared work. This task-count measure does not imply 74% labor savings or 74% autonomous client decisions. Estimate time reduction using paired baseline and observed minutes for the same task classes, and include exception handling. If a baseline week requires 40 repetitive-work hours and the instrumented week requires 18, measured time reduction is 55%, even though task automation is 74%. Review a random sample of passing records as well as every exception to detect silent drift. The principal owns the weekly error budget, while contractors own correction queues. Stop increasing intake when unresolved high-impact exceptions exceed the team's documented capacity, rather than letting attractive dashboard volume hide a growing service backlog.

Price each run as an operating unit with a defined boundary. An illustrative screening run handles one sponsor's bounded document packet and produces one reviewable research record; it excludes a full claims audit or policy placement. Budget $0.12 for compute and queue activity, $0.30 for language-model usage, $0.05 for storage allocation, and three reviewer minutes at $55 per hour, or $2.75. Total unit cost is $3.22. The model allowance could represent 60,000 input tokens at $3 per million plus 8,000 output tokens at $15 per million; these are planning rates, not a vendor quotation. Enforce token and document-size limits, and replace allowances with invoice observations monthly. At 180 runs per month, this workload costs $579.60 monthly or $6,955.20 annually. If review time doubles to six minutes, unit cost rises to $5.97 and monthly cost to $1,074.60. This sensitivity makes reviewer effort more important than shaving pennies from model tokens. Route oversized packets into a separately priced audit queue instead of absorbing unlimited work into the screening unit. Track completed, failed, and abandoned runs in the same cost denominator so unsuccessful processing remains visible. Allocate shared software and supervision separately to avoid pretending that variable run cost equals total delivery cost.

Reconcile automation spending to Formula v2.0 rather than inventing a new profit story. Conservative revenue of $120,000 less $81,600 total costs yields $38,400 owner net profit at 32%; Base revenue of $535,000 less $294,250 yields $240,750 at 45.0%; Scaled revenue of $950,000 less $399,000 yields $551,000 at 58%. These are the supplied annual scenario totals. Their revenue basis is retained PEPM advisory fees, stop-loss or TPA commissions, and earned contingent E-Mod refund splits, excluding employer claim funds and insurance premiums. Although the scorecard labels its top line gross revenue, that line is not gross employer billings or premium volume. Assess principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606 from the actual arrangement; where retained-share treatment applies, do not apply a second retention haircut to these already retained operator figures. The illustrative $6,955.20 annual screening budget fits inside Base costs, leaving $287,294.80 for all other included costs rather than increasing the scorecard expense total. Conservative and Base retain 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C, six people. The $2,000–$11,000 monthly operating-overhead range is not a substitute for fully loaded annual scenario costs. Likewise, $8,000–$45,000 startup capital and a 2–5 month first-deal interval require a separate cash runway schedule, not premature revenue recognition.

sections.heading: 4. Turn Verified Work Into Permissioned Distribution and Recoverable Growth
paragraphs: The final three mapped plays are approved benchmark publishing, partner referral routing, and high_velocity_dm_outbound_systems, the TRACK_2 High-Velocity DM Outbound & Trigger Funnels play. Together with the preceding eight, these form the chapter's 11-play operating map; the descriptive names identify local workflows rather than asserting additional catalog identifiers. Publish a source-linked renewal checklist, an illustrative NADAC calculator, and a state-specific E-Mod document checklist using reusable page templates. Each page needs an editorial owner, version date, calculation tests, and a concrete next step. Do not generate hundreds of thin locality pages or publish employer-level claims to manufacture search traffic. Use synthetic worked examples by default; any actual benchmark release requires appropriate rights, aggregation, and disclosure-risk review. A useful distribution loop starts when a CFO saves the checklist, shares it with a controller, and requests the source worksheet. Record that request as a warm signal, not permission for unrelated broadcasts. Partner routing sends an employer-authorized introduction to the appropriate licensed specialist based on state, renewal timing, and service need. Check referral compensation restrictions before promising payments to accountants or payroll firms. Keep partner attribution attached to earned operator fees rather than employer premium volume, so the loop optimizes valuable relationships instead of impressive but economically irrelevant transaction totals.

Implement high_velocity_dm_outbound_systems as an explicit signal state machine, not blind cold mass messaging. A prospect comments with the requested keyword, uses a clearly explained hand-raiser reaction, or sends an inbound message; only then may an approved integration create a pending response. A generic reaction without a clear invitation to receive a message is insufficient. Confirm platform permissions and applicable messaging rules, deduplicate the person and trigger, and send one contextual acknowledgment without an external link. Dispatch the requested link only after the prospect replies. Multi-inbox routing assigns warm conversations to the relevant authorized specialist; it must not rotate accounts to evade limits or multiply contact frequency. For an illustrative cohort, 100 valid triggers produce 60 replies, 18 qualified conversations, six meetings, and one signed client. At 100 covered lives and $8 retained PEPM, that client has a $9,600 annual fee run rate, assuming all twelve months are active; it is not $9,600 earned on signature. If content costs $200 and handling costs $300, the cohort's acquisition outlay is $500 before sales labor and onboarding. Measure those additional costs before claiming full acquisition efficiency. Reconcile trigger counts to actual delivered messages, since silent Message Request placement can make attempted dispatch look much healthier than real engagement.

Design the growth loop to fail safely. PeerFloodError, platform rate-limit responses, revoked permissions, and unexpected delivery deterioration should pause automated dispatch and alert the owner, not trigger account rotation or alternate identity creation. Preserve the prospect's requested action and route the conversation to the platform's permitted manual workflow, or wait for a fresh inbound message when no permitted continuation exists. A failed send is not permission to contact the same person through a newly discovered channel. Where commercial email is used, apply CAN-SPAM identification, postal-address, and opt-out requirements and propagate suppression across connected systems. Test webhook replay rejection, duplicate suppression, revoked CRM access, model outages, stale NADAC files, and revised bureau inputs during a monthly recovery exercise. A rollback should restore the last reviewed rule package while preserving pending work and the reason for suspension. Feed only approved, non-sensitive issue categories back into content planning: frequent renewal-date confusion can justify a better checklist, while a claimant's diagnosis cannot become marketing material. Track qualified meetings per valid trigger, retained revenue per activated client, review minutes per delivered analysis, and correction rates by source version. Expand traffic only when these measures remain stable and service capacity supports the resulting obligations. The scalable asset is a repeatable chain from evidence to trust to earned fees, not an unattended messaging machine.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 1 FT + 3 C (4 people) -> 2 FT + 4 C (6 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: Licensed Benefits and E-Mod Seats, PEPM Cohort Accounting, ERISA Compensation Disclosures, Contractor IP Assignments, and Transferable Renewal Economics
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40, Self-Funded Health, PBM & Workers' Comp Arbitrage, ranks #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 11 mapped plays become transferable assets only when licensed relationship ownership, specialist production, and evidence-based quality review operate without constant founder rescue. This chapter assigns the four-person starting pod, defines the six-person expansion, and converts weekly delivery metrics into auditable renewal economics. Canonical annual owner net profit is $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base, and $551,000 Scaled. Build around net retained advisory fees and commissions, never employer claim funds or insurance premiums. Protect the book with concentration limits, signed intellectual-property assignments, collectible accruals, and buyer-ready agreements; choose an exit only when proceeds beat the risk-adjusted value of continued distributions.

key_metrics.context: Annual agency revenue on the net retained fee and commission basis; excludes employer claim funds and insurance premiums.
key_metrics.note: 32% net margin; $38,400 annual owner net profit; 1 FT + 3 C, totaling four people.

sections.heading: 1. Assign eleven plays to four accountable seats before adding capacity
paragraphs: Treat Candidate #40's eleven mapped plays as one renewal production system, not eleven disconnected businesses. This chapter's execution map is P1 Form 5500 renewal targeting; P2 renewal and compensation diagnostics; P3 self-funded transition design; P4 captive placement analysis; P5 specific and aggregate stop-loss optimization; P6 TPA selection and implementation; P7 NADAC-based PBM repricing; P8 rebate and spread recovery; P9 reference-based pricing support and balance-bill defense coordination; P10 workers' compensation payroll and classification correction; and P11 NCCI or applicable bureau E-Mod correction and refund collection. These labels organize the stated opportunity rather than assert that every employer should buy every service. Connect each play to an employer, renewal cohort, engagement authority, deliverable, and collection event. The full-time principal owns sales, licensed recommendations, disclosures, and final client decisions. Contractor one supplies health-plan, captive, and stop-loss analysis; contractor two supplies PBM economics and reproducible data work; contractor three supplies licensed workers' compensation analysis and carrier follow-through. Keep beneficiary decisions and claim adjudication with the parties actually contracted and authorized to perform them. The four-person pod produces advice and recoveries; it does not quietly become a risk-bearing insurer, medical administrator, law firm, or custodian of employer claim funds.

Write a seat charter before recruiting a recognizable specialist. The principal must hold the applicable Life and Health and Property and Casualty producer authorities, including required business-entity licenses and appointments. A contractor performing regulated solicitation, negotiation, or sale needs their own applicable authority; the principal's license is not an umbrella permission. Contractor one delivers attachment-point comparisons, exclusions, lasers, terminal liability, and run-out analysis with source policy language. Contractor two delivers an NDC-level pricing bridge, rebate entitlement schedule, and documented treatment of specialty drugs, dispensing fees, and exclusions. Contractor three ties payroll classifications and loss runs to bureau worksheets, carrier endorsements, and employer receipts. Require an independent second look before client delivery: the principal checks commercial conclusions while the relevant specialist resolves technical exceptions. A principal unable to evaluate a specialty needs a qualified reviewer, not a signature ritual. Build this limited review purchase into engagement economics rather than silently creating another permanent seat. Contracts specify outputs, confidentiality, acceptance criteria, and delivery windows while preserving genuine independent-contractor discretion. Classification depends on actual working arrangements and applicable law, not the label printed above the signature. Reassess it whenever ongoing supervision starts resembling employee management.

Expand to two full-time employees and four contractors only after the existing pod demonstrates repeatable throughput. The second full-time seat owns account operations, renewal calendars, document completeness, reconciliation, and service recovery; obtain producer licensing before assigning regulated recommendations to that seat. The fourth contractor handles health implementation and vendor coordination, including P6 and P9 handoffs, without substituting for qualified balance-bill defense counsel. Retained outside counsel, tax preparation, and software subscriptions remain purchased services rather than hidden dedicated pod seats; budget them explicitly. Trigger expansion when eight consecutive weekly scorecards show accepted backlog beyond the principal's documented capacity, renewal deadlines remain protected, and contracted recurring contribution covers the added fixed cost under a realistic churn stress. An illustrative $90,000 annual account-operations cost requires $120,000 of incremental recurring revenue at a 75% incremental contribution rate before providing any buffer. That calculation tests a hiring decision, not a revision to the canonical scenarios. Transfer routine employer meetings using shared agendas and documented escalation rights. The principal should retain pricing and relationship accountability while another authorized person can retrieve every material commitment, explain its economics, and keep the renewal moving during a two-week founder absence without relying on personal messages.

callout.title: Build the handoff around the evidence incumbents contest
callout.body: Incumbent brokers and vendors usually challenge assumptions, authority, or timing before they challenge presentation quality. Make those three dimensions visible in every handoff.
items: Attach the actual stop-loss laser, terminal-liability, and run-out provisions to the recommendation; a premium comparison alone does not prove equivalent protection.
Freeze the NADAC reference date and NDC normalization rules with each PBM model so another analyst can reproduce the comparison after a vendor disputes it.
For E-Mod recoveries, preserve the original worksheet, corrected inputs, bureau revision, carrier endorsement, and employer receipt as separate evidence events.
Introduce the backup account owner before renewal negotiations become contentious; inherited trust is harder to manufacture during a founder's sudden absence.

sections.heading: 2. Buy accepted outputs and run a weekly exception scorecard
paragraphs: Pay contractors for accepted technical outputs rather than vague availability or projected employer savings. A workable illustrative starting schedule pays $1,200 for a complete stop-loss comparison, $900 for a reproducible PBM repricing package, and $750 for a workers' compensation correction packet. Define complexity bands and scope limits before work starts; large specialty files and multistate payroll disputes need separate quotes. Pay 80% upon documented acceptance and the remaining 20% after a ten-business-day defect window, subject to the contract and applicable payment rules. A contractor who performed the agreed analysis should not finance a carrier's unrelated payment delay. Licensed commission participation, where permitted, belongs in a separate written schedule with required disclosures; unlicensed analytics vendors should not receive disguised placement commissions. For budgeting illustrations, reserve $36,000 annually for the three contractors in Conservative, $96,000 in Base, and $168,000 for four contractors in Scaled. These are allocations inside canonical expenses, not incremental deductions from the published owner profits. Quote each engagement against its available contribution and stop accepting work that requires uncompensated expert rescue. Require correction of attributable defects without charging the client twice, but distinguish changed scope from poor original workmanship.

Use a Friday scorecard that exposes denominators and unresolved exceptions, not an attractive collection of percentages. Track qualified employer conversations, authorized data packages, proposals delivered, bound or signed engagements, and first cash receipts as separate funnel stages. Define a qualified employer as an identified decision-maker with a relevant renewal date, workable group profile, and permission to discuss the engagement. For production, target acknowledgment within one business day, completeness review within two, and technical delivery within the agreed window after complete inputs arrive. Record client-caused pauses separately rather than resetting clocks invisibly. An illustrative service objective is at least 95% on-time accepted deliverables and at least 98% first-pass accuracy on explicitly defined critical checks; disclose counts because one defect in five jobs is not comparable with one in fifty. Track stop-loss coverage exceptions, disputed PBM assumptions, and rejected E-Mod submissions by age and owner. Escalate any missing effective-date protection immediately, regardless of a green average. Weekly meetings should end with named corrective actions, promised dates, and the financial exposure of each open item. Keep contractor performance review focused on agreed results and service obligations rather than prescribing unnecessary daily supervision that undermines the intended independent relationship.

Concentration belongs on the same weekly page as delivery because a seemingly efficient book can hide one fragile dependency. Set a maximum of 25% of trailing-twelve-month recognized revenue from any single employer controlled group and 25% from any economically distinct commission-paying counterparty group. Aggregate affiliates rather than treating separate carrier entities as independent risks. Measure the next-twelve-month contracted revenue forecast and receivables alongside those historical ratios. Also cap any single carrier, TPA, or PBM dependency at 25% of the recurring revenue that its withdrawal would interrupt, even when employers pay the operator directly. These are portfolio objectives, not reasons to place an employer into an inferior arrangement. A startup with one employer necessarily exceeds the limit; show the breach openly, prohibit discretionary expansion of that exposure, and build a dated diversification plan. Do not call the book exit-ready until the limits actually hold. Recalculate revenue retention by renewal cohort, separating employer departures, employee-count changes, pricing changes, and new recovery wins. Stress the loss of the largest customer and the largest counterparty independently and together where exposures overlap. Fund fixed commitments from stressed recurring contribution, not from this month's unusually large contingent refund receipt.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the weekly evidence set
sop_steps.action: Export CRM stages, engagement tickets, recognized revenue, receivables, and contractor acceptance records each Friday.
sop_steps.detail: Use consistent cutoffs and engagement identifiers; retain the underlying export so later corrections remain traceable.

sop_steps.title: Reconcile metrics to source events
sop_steps.action: Have the principal or account-operations owner tie every scorecard numerator and denominator to the frozen records.
sop_steps.detail: Separate contingent estimates from earned fees, document paused work, and aggregate affiliated customers and counterparties.

sop_steps.action: Prioritize effective-date protection, material calculation errors, overdue collections, and concentration breaches before ordinary backlog.

sop_steps.action: Confirm corrections, release accepted contractor payments, and update capacity commitments for the following week.
sop_steps.detail: Compare actual engagement contribution with quoted contribution and suspend repeatable loss-making scope until pricing or production changes.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile retained revenue, accruals, and contractor ownership monthly
paragraphs: Preserve the scorecard's economic boundary before discussing a multiple. Conservative revenue of $120,000 less $81,600 of expenses produces $38,400 owner profit at 32%; Base revenue of $535,000 less $294,250 produces $240,750 at 45.0%; Scaled revenue of $950,000 less $399,000 produces $551,000 at 58%. The first two cases use one full-time principal and three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time seats and four contractors. Although the source scenarios label their top line gross revenue, the defined basis is agency revenue from net retained advisory fees, stop-loss and TPA commissions, and contingent E-Mod refund splits. Employer premiums, claim deposits, pharmacy spending, and refund principal never become operator revenue merely because a dashboard displays them. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to each contractual promise and document the retained-share bridge wherever collections include amounts belonging to another party. Do not apply an invented second haircut to the canonical revenue. Under the illustrative contractor budgets above, remaining expense allowances are $45,600, $198,250, and $231,000 respectively. Those amounts must cover all other included operating costs; they are not additional owner distributions. Reconcile actual ledger classifications before comparing owner profit with buyer-adjusted earnings, because the scorecard alone does not specify every compensation or accounting convention.

Maintain accrual schedules by employer, policy year, renewal cohort, revenue stream, and counterparty rather than relying on deposits in QuickBooks Online or Xero. A PEPM advisory engagement earns revenue as the contracted service is delivered using reconciled eligible lives and the agreed billing definition. For example, 500 covered employees at $6 retained PEPM produce $3,000 for a fully earned service month, not $36,000 on signature day. Commission recognition follows the actual contract, performance obligations, cancellation provisions, and applicable variable consideration assessment, with clawback exposure separately supported. For a $100,000 employer refund carrying a 20% contractual recovery fee, the operator's fee opportunity is $20,000; the employer's $100,000 recovery is not agency sales. Recognize contingent fees only when the performance obligation and variable-consideration requirements are satisfied, including the assessment of significant reversal risk. A promising bureau recalculation is not automatically an earned, collectible carrier refund. Reconcile opening receivables plus recognized fees less cash, credits, and write-offs to closing receivables monthly. Separate unbilled earned amounts from speculative pipeline. Accrue accepted contractor services in the same close rather than inflating a strong month by postponing invoices. Preserve cohort-level acquisition costs and service hours so a buyer can distinguish durable renewal contribution from founder-subsidized delivery.

Transferability also requires ownership of the machinery that generates the numbers. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), a transfer of copyright ownership generally requires a signed writing by the owner or their authorized agent. Obtain assignments covering commissioned scripts, calculation templates, documentation, and other copyrightable deliverables; do not assume that paying an independent contractor creates ownership or that every commission qualifies as work made for hire. Schedule preexisting contractor tools separately and secure an adequate continuing license where assignment is unavailable. Copyright assignments do not transfer employer records, PBM confidential material, bureau data rights, or third-party software licenses. Establish separate permissions for each. Keep source repositories, administrative accounts, and recovery evidence under organization-controlled identities with least-privilege access and tested offboarding. Where the operator or contractor acts as a HIPAA business associate or subcontractor, execute the applicable agreements and implement required safeguards before sharing protected health information. A buyer data room starts with aggregated operating metrics and redacted contracts, not identifiable claims files. Document assignment restrictions, carrier appointments, producer registrations, and business-entity change requirements in a transfer register. An asset sale does not automatically transfer every license, appointment, client authorization, or vendor contract. Price unresolved transfer work before entering exclusivity.

callout.title: Verify four transfer conditions before promising a buyer continuity
callout.body: Treat each condition as an evidence requirement. Unresolved items affect transaction structure, timing, and price rather than disappearing into an optimistic earnings multiple.
items: Verify active producer and business-entity authorities, required appointments, applicable TPA requirements, and ERISA section 408(b)(2) compensation disclosures for the actual services performed.

Verify that each material engagement and vendor agreement identifies assignment restrictions, change-of-control provisions, termination rights, and the party responsible for obtaining required permissions.
Verify signed contractor IP assignments or sufficient continuing licenses, organization-controlled repositories, and written treatment of preexisting tools and restricted source materials.

Verify reconciled trailing-twelve-month revenue, contingent-fee support, concentration at or below 25% for each defined exposure, and a normalized earnings bridge that includes founder replacement costs.

sections.heading: 4. Underwrite an exit multiple against transferable earnings and retained cash
paragraphs: Value the transferable business, not the founder's ability to work indefinitely without replacement. A small owner-operated advisory book may be discussed using seller's discretionary earnings, while a larger professionally serviced book is more naturally assessed on normalized EBITDA or retained recurring revenue. Those denominators are not interchangeable. For preliminary negotiation modeling, use illustrative ranges of 2.0 to 3.5 times normalized SDE for a founder-dependent microbusiness and 3.5 to 5.0 times normalized EBITDA for a more transferable small specialist operation. These are underwriting assumptions, not observed transaction comparables or an assurance that a buyer will bid. Obtain current comparable transactions with matching size, revenue quality, retention, and deal structure before setting an asking price. Pure recurring books can also be discussed using revenue multiples, but that shortcut becomes dangerous when contingent refund fees dominate or service intensity varies. A strategic buyer may credit distribution synergies, yet the seller should not capitalize savings the buyer has neither validated nor agreed to share. The defensible premium comes from documented renewal retention, clean rights, diversified counterparties, accountable service ownership, and low founder dependence. A high annual margin achieved by skipping coverage review or contractor accruals should reduce confidence rather than increase the multiple.

Build the earnings bridge explicitly before multiplying anything. For an illustration only, assume canonical owner profit is measured before an additional market-rate replacement for the working principal and that interest, income taxes, depreciation, and amortization require no further bridge adjustments. Deduct $100,000 of fully loaded replacement cost from Base owner profit of $240,750 to obtain $140,750 of illustrative normalized earnings. Deduct $130,000 from Scaled owner profit of $551,000 to obtain $421,000. If actual expenses already include that replacement role, remove the duplicate deduction; if additional normalizations exist, rebuild the bridge. At 3.5 to 5.0 times, the illustrative enterprise values are $492,625 to $703,750 for Base and $1,473,500 to $2,105,000 for Scaled. These calculations do not change the canonical profit cases. Conservative's $38,400 cannot support the illustrative $100,000 replacement cost, making a self-operating EBITDA valuation inappropriate without a different cost structure or buyer synergy. Bridge enterprise value to seller proceeds through actual debt, cash treatment, working-capital adjustments, fees, escrows, and contingent payments. Never present the top end of enterprise value as cash available at closing. Show buyer assumptions separately from the operator's verified historical results.

Use the same evidence package to choose between selling and retaining a durable cash-producing book. A buyer's headline price may contain a substantial earnout tied to renewals they will influence after closing. Define retained revenue, excluded cancellations, producer reassignment, pricing changes, reporting access, dispute resolution, and collection timing in the purchase agreement. Consider an illustrative $1,700,000 enterprise-value offer with 70% paid at closing and 30% contingent: the stated components are $1,190,000 and $510,000 before other adjustments, not $1,700,000 of immediate liquidity. Compare expected net proceeds with a discounted distribution model that includes founder replacement, maintenance spending, working capital, taxes, and losses from concentrated customers or counterparties. Do not compare a pretax sale headline with after-tax annual distributions. For the retained-book option, maintain a cash reserve calibrated to payroll, contractor commitments, clawbacks, and collection delays; test a minimum three-month operating-cost buffer against actual seasonality. Run the founder-absence exercise twice annually and refresh the transfer register after each renewal. Quarterly buyer readiness should improve service and liquidity even if no sale occurs. The pod has earned a premium only when another qualified operator can preserve its economics without recreating the founder's undocumented judgment or inheriting avoidable counterparty surprises.

chapters.pull_quote: A premium book is one another qualified operator can renew, reconcile, and defend without borrowing the founder's memory.

chapters.title: The First 30-Day Launch Sprint & Kill / Fix / Scale Gates
chapters.subtitle: A Four-Person ERISA, Pass-Through PBM, Stop-Loss and NCCI Audit Pod: Daily Deliverables, Retained-Fee Economics and Evidence-Based Spending Limits
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #40, ranked #08 of 42 with a 93/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, requires a controlled evidence sprint, not an immediate insurance placement. This chapter sequences 11 mapped plays through one full-time operator and three specialist contractors, from Form 5500 targeting through PBM reconciliation and Workers' Comp refund recovery. Days 1–30 establish licensed authority, secure intake, reproducible analyses and two decision-ready proposals under a $6,000 cash-disbursement ceiling. Day 30/60/90 thresholds separate channel failure from repairable evidence gaps and earned expansion. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $38,400 Conservative, $240,750 Base and $551,000 Scaled; employer premiums, claim funds and recovered employer dollars never become operator revenue merely by passing through a calculation.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Build the Licensed Pod and Select One Entry Wedge
paragraphs: Start with one employer segment, one home jurisdiction and one accountable producer, rather than advertising three unrelated savings promises. Assign the full-time operator prospect selection, employer interviews, compensation disclosure, proposal ownership and cash control. Contractor C1 supplies benefits actuarial and stop-loss analysis; C2 handles PBM contract interpretation and prescription repricing; C3 handles Workers' Comp classification, experience-rating review and carrier correction packets. Verify actual qualifications before assigning work: an analyst designation does not confer producer authority, and a producer license does not authorize every TPA activity. Obtain narrowly scoped outside counsel when required, charged to the launch budget rather than represented as another permanent pod seat. Day 1 produces a state-and-service authority matrix covering individual and business-entity licensing, lines of authority, appointments and any administrator registration. Use NIPR and the relevant insurance department to verify records, not a contractor's email assertion. New York Insurance Law §2102 provides a concrete example of prohibited unlicensed producer activity; other states require separate checks. Until the necessary authority is active, restrict work to internal preparation and activities the applicable jurisdiction permits. Do not solicit, negotiate or accept transaction compensation on the assumption that a future license will cure today's conduct.

Use an explicit eleven-play work map so adjacent opportunities do not become eleven simultaneous engagements. P01 is Form 5500 renewal targeting; P02 is broker compensation and incumbent-contract reconstruction; P03 is self-funded plan feasibility; P04 is captive stop-loss suitability; P05 is specific and aggregate stop-loss restructuring; P06 is TPA fee and service procurement; P07 is NADAC-referenced PBM repricing; P08 is rebate and pass-through reconciliation; P09 is reference-based pricing feasibility with balance-bill defense; P10 is Workers' Comp payroll and classification correction; P11 is experience-modification review and contingent refund recovery. These are the chapter's operational labels for the eleven mapped plays, not eleven promised revenue streams. P01 and P02 support every account; select either the benefits branch or the Workers' Comp branch as the first paid wedge. Defer P04 and P09 unless employer size, funding tolerance, contractual protection and qualified specialists support them. On Days 2–4, screen forty employers with roughly 100–500 covered employees and a documented renewal or audit window. Use public DOL EFAST2 filings, employer websites and permitted business outreach. Treat Schedule A and Schedule C as historical clues: filing lag, reporting exemptions and plan structure can leave important commercial relationships outside either schedule.

Set the first-month disbursement ceiling at $6,000 against the published $8,000–$45,000 startup range. Allocate $1,400 to licensing, insurance and specialist contract review, $600 to secure systems, $2,400 to contractor analysis, $600 to targeted outreach and $1,000 to contingencies. These are planning envelopes, not vendor quotations; if required licensing or coverage costs more, reduce scope before committing funds. At the $8,000 capitalization floor, leave $2,000 untouched and sign no automatic contractor renewals. Create a weekly ledger separating cash paid, obligations already incurred, collectible invoices and speculative success fees. Preserve sufficient cash for the next thirty days of unavoidable obligations before releasing any new discretionary purchase. The launch ceiling includes setup purchases and does not replace the volume's $2,000–$11,000 monthly operating-expense range. By Day 5, configure Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace under appropriate contractual terms, MFA, restricted folders and named account access. Begin with aggregate census and contract documents; receive identifiable claims only after the applicable privacy role, business associate agreement and permitted purpose are established. Days 6–7 rehearse intake with synthetic records, test contractor access removal and produce the first scored prospect list. No employer evidence should enter personal email or an unapproved public model endpoint.
